Cadiz Inc. is a California water and land company developing the Mojave Groundwater Bank in San Bernardino County. **[Fact]** The company owns roughly **46,000 acres** in the Mojave Desert with permitted rights to conserve **2.5 million acre-feet** of groundwater over 50 years (average **50,000 acre-feet per year**) and to bank up to **one million acre-feet** of imported water in the underlying aquifer (`investor-documents/sec-edgar/10-K_20260331_rpt20251231_acc0001437749_26_010517.htm`, Item 1). **[Fact]** Cadiz also owns a **220-mile** idle natural-gas pipeline acquired in 2021 that management plans to convert for water conveyance, plus **43 miles** of pipeline right-of-way entitlements. **[Fact]** Operating revenue today comes mainly from **ATEC** water-filtration equipment sales (**$14.5 million** in FY2025), alfalfa farming on **760 acres**, and agricultural leases. **[Fact]** The company formed **Mojave Water Infrastructure Company LLC (MWI)** in December 2024 to finance an estimated **$1.25 to $1.5 billion** buildout with public, tribal, and private equity partners. **[Fact]** As of May 11, 2026, **84,086,286** common shares were outstanding (NASDAQ: CDZI).

### Moat (Munger)

**Unproven.** If constructed and operated, a permitted groundwater bank with dedicated pipeline interconnects to California aqueducts would resemble a localized water toll. Today there is no scaled delivery, heavy reliance on capital partners, and a long history of shareholder dilution. Competitive alternatives include state storage (Diamond Valley Lake), Colorado River allocations, and conservation mandates. Moat assessment upgrades only after durable contracted cash flow at the wellhead.

**Dhando (Pabrai):** **Partial.** Permitted water and pipeline assets provide an economic floor in success scenarios, but **$78 million** of debt, ongoing losses, and ATM dilution mean common equity can still be impaired if financing slips.

**Stance proposal:** **Watch.** Base annual return is below our **~15%** hurdle; accumulate only after binding MWI equity and a dated Northern Pipeline conversion schedule.

**Bear vs base:** Bear assumes financing failure and continued dilution; base assumes partial MWI close and initial **~20,000 AFY** deliveries.

## Executive summary
Cadiz owns permitted Mojave groundwater storage and a 220-mile pipeline path, plus ATEC filter sales (**$16.3 million** FY2025 revenue). The company still loses money (**$31.1 million** net FY2025) and carries **$78.3 million** of debt while raising **~$451 million** through project vehicle MWI (Lytton **$51 million** facility signed October 2025). **We expect 6.2% per year** over seven years to a **$6.00** per share payoff if partial financing and pipeline conversion proceed. Dhando is **partial**; moat **unproven**. Stance **watch** until binding MWI equity and an in-service date.

## Why the market might be wrong
The stock may trade as a perennial "water project" story with dilution overhang, while filings show concrete permits, contracted offtake, and a capital structure taking shape around MWI. **[Fact]** In 2024 Cadiz signed agreements for **21,275 acre-feet per year** of supply to be delivered via the Northern Pipeline, with filing guidance that initial throughput may be **20,000 to 23,000 AFY** after value engineering (`10-K FY2025`, Item 1). **[Fact]** Supply pricing is estimated to net Cadiz approximately **$850 per acre-foot** (2024 dollars, inflation-adjusted) at the wellhead after shared capital and operating costs. **[Inference]** GAAP book value (**~$0.28** per share at December 31, 2025) carries land and pipeline at historical cost and does not capitalize the permitted water bank, so price-to-book screens understate the asset option. **[Inference]** Predictive attribute: **dormant asset** plus **equity yield curve**. Institutional holders may avoid the name until MWI financing closes and water deliveries begin, creating a timing gap between permit value and run-rate cash.

## Risks & inversion
**Primary risk:** MWI fails to secure **~$451 million** of equity and complementary debt/grants, forcing more dilution or asset sales while debt matures.

**Inversion checklist:**

- If Lytton draw and PE commitments do not bind, can Cadiz fund operations for 24 months without punitive equity issuance?
- If Northern Pipeline throughput caps at **20,000 AFY**, does contracted **21,275 AFY** require Southern Pipeline capital earlier than modeled?
- If ATEC growth slows, is there any path to profitability without Mojave Bank?
- If secured debt maturities slip past June 2027, does Heerema relationship force dilutive restructuring?

**Lens failure mode (asset):** Treating GAAP book (**~$0.28** per share) as a floor ignores that fair value lives in permits and pipeline routes not fully marked on the balance sheet, while **debt exceeds equity**. The correct floor is probability-weighted project success, not book.

## Business & moat

This is a permanent-capital equity wrapper, not an operating company. DWS selects Central and Eastern European stocks; shareholders own a slice of that portfolio minus fees (net expense ratio about 1.26%). The liquid engine today is concentrated in Poland and Hungary (financials, energy, industrials). That book is Level 1 and is what reported net asset value reflects.

The Russia sleeve is the structural oddity. The July 2025 schedule still lists Sberbank, Gazprom, Lukoil, Magnit, Alrosa, and several depositary-receipt lines, all at zero, with footnote that valuation uses significant unobservable inputs. Cost basis on that sleeve was about $30.7 million when fund net assets were about $100 million. Some non-sanctioned depositary receipts were sold privately in 2024; remaining local shares and sanctioned receipts stay stuck. That is a classic option-scan hit: the accounting mark is not the economic claim.

There is no product moat at the fund level. Durability lives in the underlying issuers and in closed-end structure (no daily redemptions). Alignment tools include open-market repurchases when shares trade below reported net asset value. Fees and any future tender/liquidation friction are the structural drags.

Historical cost of the Russia sleeve on the July 2025 schedule was about $30.7 million (~$4.7 per share at today’s share count). That is a floor-of-sorts on *paid-in* capital, not a market mark.

## [HUMAN REVIEW]

- Set `realization_probability_base` for the Russia sleeve (still 0% in base).
- Refresh share counts from the latest N-PORT / N-CSR (PH3 is 31 Jul 2025).
- Decide ADR/GDR mapping rules before trusting the ~$30 full-proxy NAV.

#### Look-through snapshot

| Sleeve | Role in reported NAV | Role in economic view |
|--------|----------------------|------------------------|
| Poland / Hungary / other liquid equities | Marked Level 1; drives reported NAV | Floor |
| Cash / equivalents | Included | Floor |
| Russia equities (schedule still lists names) | **$0 since 14 Mar 2022** | Option / illustration only until human sets recovery probability |

## Executive summary

CEE is a shadow-net-asset-value idea disguised as a near-par closed-end fund. At about $20.48 versus reported net asset value of about $21.32, the stock looks only a few percent cheap. That comparison ignores Russia. Using the last detailed schedule (July 2025) and current Moscow exchange prints, a mark-to-market illustration adds roughly $5 to $9 per share of Russian equity value before any friction. That implies an economic net asset value near the mid-$20s to about $30, or a mid-20s to low-30s percent discount to price. The base case in this report still values Russia at zero until a human sets a recovery probability, so the published base return is only about **4% per year** from liquid-book growth with a sticky reported discount. The asymmetric payoff (Pabrai dhando) is the Russia option: downside is mostly the liquid Central European book and fees; upside is any non-zero recovery. Stance stays **watch** until recovery odds and share-count freshness are reviewed.

## Terms (this report)

| Term | Meaning here |
|------|----------------|
| Reported net asset value | Sponsor NAV with Russia at zero |
| Economic / mark-to-market NAV | Illustration adding Moscow marks to the Russia sleeve |
| Dhando | Asymmetric payoff: bounded liquid book vs open-ended Russia option |
| Shadow NAV | Economic value above reported NAV because of zero marks |

#### Option scan

| # | Question | If yes |
|---|----------|--------|
| 1 | Does reported net asset value misstate a material sleeve? | **Yes.** Russia at zero since 14 Mar 2022. Treatment: `fund_nav_overlay` / probability-weighted; **base case stays zero** until human sets recovery probability. |
| 2 | Undeveloped or dormant asset priced at zero? | **Yes.** Same Russia sleeve. Illustration only in Valuation. |
| 3 | Buyback / tender catalyst? | Yes, recurring repurchase authorization when at a discount to *reported* NAV. Secondary. |
| 4 | Private stakes below fair value? | Not the main story (liquid CE book is marked). |
| 5 | Embedded product option already in cash flows? | No. |

### Mental models

- **Accounting mark ≠ economic claim:** reported net asset value can be honest under the rules and still miss the investment.
- **Free option on a solvent floor:** liquid Central European book bounds the bear; Russia is the open-ended sleeve.
- **Do not confuse near-par to reported NAV with fair value** when a disclosed sleeve sits at zero.

## What this business is

The Central and Eastern Europe Fund is a New York–listed closed-end fund run by DWS. It owns a portfolio of mostly Polish and Hungarian equities (banks, energy, insurers, retailers) plus a frozen Russian equity sleeve. Since 14 March 2022 the fund has carried those Russian holdings at zero under sanctions and capital controls, even though the share counts are still disclosed. The publicly reported net asset value therefore describes only the liquid book. The share price usually tracks that reported figure closely.

section: Why the market might be wrong
text:
## Why the market might be wrong

The interesting mispricing is not the thin discount to reported net asset value. It is that reported net asset value itself may understate economic ownership by writing the entire Russian book to zero. The predictive attribute is a Level-3 / sanctions zero mark: local Moscow prices still exist for many names, but a United States fund cannot freely realize them. If any path to recovery, private sale, or eventual unblocking opens, that sleeve is a free (or cheap) option on top of a solvent Central European equity portfolio. Buybacks when the fund trades below reported net asset value are a secondary catalyst, not the main edge.

The Central and Eastern Europe Fund is a New York–listed closed-end fund run by DWS. It owns a portfolio of mostly Polish and Hungarian equities (banks, energy, insurers, retailers) plus a frozen Russian equity sleeve. Since 14 March 2022 the fund has carried those Russian holdings at zero under sanctions and capital controls, even though the share counts are still disclosed. The publicly reported net asset value therefore describes only the liquid book. The share price usually tracks that reported figure closely.

The interesting mispricing is not the thin discount to reported net asset value. It is that reported net asset value itself may understate economic ownership by writing the entire Russian book to zero. The predictive attribute is a Level-3 / sanctions zero mark: local Moscow prices still exist for many names, but a United States fund cannot freely realize them. If any path to recovery, private sale, or eventual unblocking opens, that sleeve is a free (or cheap) option on top of a solvent Central European equity portfolio. Buybacks when the fund trades below reported net asset value are a secondary catalyst, not the main edge.

At **$267.25** (Yahoo close 2026-08-04), our base case annual return is **-27.4%** per year over seven years on filing-normalized owner cash of **$3.57 per share**, net of **$15.8 billion** of net debt. Constellation operates America's largest nuclear fleet (~55 GW) and signed a **20-year** Microsoft power purchase agreement to restart Three Mile Island Unit 1 as the Crane Clean Energy Center. FY2025 revenue was **$25.5 billion**, but owner cash was only **$1.29 billion** after **$2.95 billion** of capital spending. The January 2026 Calpine acquisition roughly doubled quarterly revenue versus the prior year but added debt and integration complexity. Component proof base value is **$28.53 per share**. Moat is **unproven** pending durable contract economics; dhando is **partial** because asset quality is real but price embeds optionality. Proposed stance: **watch**.

## Why the market might be wrong
The market may be capitalizing **scarce nuclear capacity and AI-driven firm-power contracts** (including the Microsoft agreement to restart Crane Clean Energy Center) while underweighting **$17 billion of debt**, **capital spending that consumed 70% of operating cash flow in FY2025**, and **normalized owner cash of only $3.57 per share**. **[Inference]** At **$253.50**, the stock requires roughly **20%+ sustained owner-cash growth** and a mid-teens exit multiple just to break even on a Lawrence-style seven-year path, far above what FY2025 filings support. **[Inference]** Calpine adds scale and ERCOT exposure but also integration risk and incremental leverage that are not yet reflected in a clean owner-cash run-rate.

#### IRR arithmetic (show your work)

How we calculated the annual return (mechanical sync from `valuation.json` calculation proof):

1. Growth from reinvestment = reinvestment rate × incremental return on capital (base: 35% × 18% = 6.3% per year).
2. Year-one owner earnings = starting owner earnings × (1 + growth).
3. Distributable cash each year = owner earnings × (1 − reinvestment rate).
4. Present value of seven years of distributable cash at the discount rate.
5. Terminal value = year-seven owner earnings × terminal multiple; discounted to present.
6. Enterprise value = sum of present values.
7. Equity value = enterprise value + cash − long-term debt.
8. Value per share = equity value ÷ shares (**$502.23** base component value).
9. Annual return at today's price: **8.57% per year** at **$282.49** (contract: `valuation_contract.json`).

section: Why the market might be wrong
text:
## Why the market might be wrong
The market may be anchoring on **Medicare Advantage utilization noise** and **PBM legislative headlines** while underweighting **Evernorth's specialty-pharmacy mix**, **employer stickiness**, and **buyback-funded per-share compounding** at a price below our component base value. **[Inference]** At **$283.94**, the stock trades at a discount to a filing-based owner-earnings reinvestment model once long-term debt is taken from the FY2025 10-K rather than a stale 2018 tag; the gap is not a hidden-asset story but a **quality-at-a-discount** setup if medical trends normalize.

## Risks & inversion

| Risk | Mechanism | Severity | Falsifier / monitor |
|------|-----------|----------|---------------------|
| Medicare Advantage utilization | Higher-than-expected medical costs compress insurance margin | High | Two quarters of MA MLR below guidance |
| PBM regulation | Spread compression on pharmacy benefit economics | High | Final rule text vs Evernorth margin disclosure |
| Medical cost trend | Premium increases lag claim inflation | Medium | Commercial risk-adjusted margin decline in 10-Q |
| Debt/refinancing | **$31B** long-term stack rolls in higher-rate environment | Medium | Weighted average coupon stable in 10-K debt footnote |
| Goodwill / intangibles | Large acquisition goodwill from Express Scripts era | Medium | Impairment charge in 10-K or 8-K |
| Regulatory capital | Insurance subsidiaries must hold statutory surplus | Medium | RBC ratios stable in statutory filing excerpts |
| Pharmacy receivable cycle | Working-capital swings can depress quarterly OCF | Low | OCF conversion stable vs net income over four quarters |

**Primary risk:** Medical-cost trend and Medicare Advantage rate resets can outrun premium increases, compressing Cigna Healthcare earnings faster than Evernorth pharmacy growth offsets.

**Inversion (what would make us wrong to watch):** Two consecutive quarters with consolidated adjusted income growth above **8%** and share count down **2%+** year over year would force reinvestment-rate and stance reassessment.

**Lens failure mode:** Treating consolidated operating cash flow as fully distributable ignores regulatory capital needs in insurance subsidiaries and periodic working-capital swings in pharmacy receivables.

| Field | Value | Evidence |
|-------|-------|----------|
| Archetype | compounder | Integrated insurer + PBM at scale |
| Cycle | mid | Post-COVID utilization normalization; MA rate cycles |
| Lawrence bucket | multi_sided | Plans, employers, pharmacies, manufacturers |

The Cigna Group earns fees and premiums across a two-sided health ecosystem: Evernorth captures pharmacy and care economics; Cigna Healthcare captures underwriting spread and admin fees.

#### Catalyst path

- **Base catalyst** (2–4 years): Normalized medical-cost trend and steady Evernorth script growth restore mid-single-digit owner-cash growth.

## Why the market might be wrong
The market may treat CKX as a stagnant micro-cap land stub whose earnings spike was a one-time land sale, missing the ongoing strategic-alternatives process and the cash-rich balance sheet relative to run-rate royalties. **[Fact]** FY2025 net income was **$3.0 million** (**$1.47** per share) but included a **$3,557,868** land-sale gain; operating profit excluding that gain was roughly **$83,000**. **[Fact]** Cash and equivalents totaled **$18.0 million** at **December 31, 2025** (**~$8.78** per share) against stockholders equity of **~$10.47** per share at **March 31, 2026**. **[Inference]** At **~$10.59** (June 10, 2026), the stock trades near GAAP book while cash alone covers a large fraction of the quote, with co-owned acreage and royalty streams as a free option. **[Inference]** Predictive attribute: **dormant asset** plus **market structure discount** (thin float, no analyst coverage, no dividend screen inclusion).

## Risks & inversion
**Primary risk:** The strategic-alternatives process fails to produce a value-maximizing transaction, leaving shareholders with a depleting royalty stream, co-owner gridlock on the **5,533** net co-owned acres, and elevated G&A relative to **~$84K** normalized operating profit.

- **Inversion:** If management continues **~$1,316/acre** land sales on additional wholly-owned or partitionable tracts and redeploys cash via accretive repurchases, per-share value could compound even without a full company sale.
- Co-owner unanimity requirement may block timber harvests, leases, or bulk sales that would otherwise unlock value.
- Hurricane damage (e.g., **Hurricane Laura 2020** damaged **~33%** of standing timber) can interrupt royalties and timber income.
- Oil and gas price declines reduce royalty checks without CKX operating leverage to cut costs.
- Micro-cap illiquidity can widen bid-ask spreads and trap patient capital without a catalyst.

**Lens failure mode (asset payoff):** If November 2025 acreage was uniquely valuable timberland not representative of co-owned marsh or undivided interests, the apparent acreage option is smaller than the sale comp implies and the asset lens collapses to a low-yield cash bond.

## Executive summary
CKX is a debt-free Louisiana land and royalty vehicle: **7,023** net acres, **$18 million** cash, and three operating segments (oil and gas royalties, timber, surface rents). The November 2025 sale of **6,548** acres at roughly **$1,316** per acre demonstrated management's willingness to monetize wholly-owned land inside an active strategic-review process. Normalized owner cash is roughly **$0.22** per share from FY2025 operating cash flow, far below headline earnings inflated by the land gain. Our base case annual return is **3.7%** per year on a dated payoff path to **~$15.50** per share over seven years, anchored on cash floor plus partial acreage monetization. Cash per share provides a strong partial dhando floor, but co-owner governance friction, depleting royalties, and process uncertainty keep moat unproven. We propose **watch** pending a definitive strategic outcome or repeatable per-acre monetization above run-rate cash yield.

## What this business is
CKX Lands, Inc. is a Louisiana land and mineral royalty company listed on NYSE American. **[Fact]** The company owns and manages approximately **7,023 net acres** across Louisiana parishes, earning passive income from oil and gas royalties, timber sales, surface easements, and occasional land sales. **[Fact]** CKX does not explore for or operate oil and gas wells; third-party operators produce on leased acreage while CKX collects royalties ranging from **0.0045%** to **7.62%** across **20** producing fields. **[Fact]** The company has **two** part-time employees, **no** debt, and **no** dividend program. **[Fact]** Following a **November 18, 2025** sale of **6,548** wholly-owned acres for **$8,618,022** cash, roughly **90%** of remaining net acres are co-owned undivided interests requiring unanimous co-owner consent for major decisions. **[Fact]** The Board has evaluated strategic alternatives since **August 2023**, including potential sale of the company or additional asset dispositions.

## Risks & inversion
**Primary risk:** Hashprice falls faster than CleanSpark can cut power cost or upgrade machines, compressing owner cash while debt and converts remain.

Additional risks:
- **$1.79 billion** long-term debt (March 2026) plus **$636 million** zero-coupon converts and bitcoin-collateral credit lines (10-K liquidity section).
- GAAP earnings swing with ASC 350-60 bitcoin fair-value marks (**$471 million** YTD loss H1 FY2026).
- AI data center build requires heavy upfront capex with revenue lag (10-K liquidity discussion).
- Customer/supplier concentration on Bitmain ASICs and mining pools.

**Lens failure mode (operating + optionality):** Using Adjusted EBITDA (**$823 million**) as owner cash while ignoring that it embeds bitcoin mark dynamics; treating FY2025 hash scale as permanent without H1 FY2026 revenue decline.

**Inversion:** What would make this work? Sustained BTC above **$100k**, hash share stable above **4%**, AI hosting contracts on existing **1 GW** footprint, and convert stack refinanced without massive dilution.

## Why the market might be wrong
**Predictive attribute:** complexity discount (GAAP earnings dominated by bitcoin fair-value marks, convertibles, and an unproven AI hosting pivot).

**[Inference]** The market may treat CleanSpark as a levered bitcoin proxy (rewarding FY2025 hash scale-up) while underpricing hashprice compression already visible in H1 FY2026 filings. **[Fact]** H1 FY2026 mining revenue was **$317.6 million**, down **7.7%** year over year despite a larger fleet. **[Fact]** Q2 FY2026 GAAP operating loss was **$345.7 million** in the quarter, driven by **$224.1 million** net fair-value loss on bitcoin transactions and measurement. **[Inference]** Conversely, bears may ignore the **$316 million** of FY2025 owner cash (operating cash flow minus capital spending) and the strategic value of **1 gigawatt-class** power footprint if AI hosting converts.

---

#### Moat (Munger)

**Unproven.** CleanSpark has real assets (power contracts, immersion sites, fleet density), but bitcoin mining is a commodity toll on electricity and silicon. Incentive-caused bias favors aggressive hash growth and convert issuance, which helped scale but now magnifies mark-to-market volatility and dilution.

**Primary metric (stance gate):** Lawrence ten-year base **7.5% per year** on **$0.99 per share** starting owner cash. **Bull sensitivity:** **19.7% per year** (`scenarios.bull`). Total synthesis **12.5%** is context-only (persona blend); stance uses Lawrence **7.5%**.

## What this business is
CME Group is the world's largest listed derivatives marketplace: futures and options on interest rates, equity indexes, foreign exchange, energy, metals, and agricultural products, plus clearing, market data, and collateral services. **[Fact]** Customers pay transaction, clearing, and market-data fees; CME does not take directional market risk on customer positions. **[Fact]** FY2025 total revenues were **$6,520.6 million**, operating income **$4,229.5 million**, and net income **$4,072.2 million** (`investor-documents/sec-edgar/10-K_20260226_rpt20251231_acc0001156375_26_000009.htm`). **[Fact]** Q1 2026 revenues were **$1,880.1 million** with operating income **$1,309.7 million** and net income **$1,154.3 million** (`investor-documents/sec-edgar/10-Q_20260424_rpt20260331_acc0001156375_26_000020.htm`). Pillars 1 and 4 are **cyclical** (macro volatility and new product adoption). Pillars 2 and 3 are **structural** (clearing network and data subscription). Peer context: ICE and Cboe share croupier economics; CME is more concentrated in rates and equity indexes.

**Fieldwork / management:** None this period. Proxy documents executive compensation (`DEF 14A_20260323_rpt20251231_acc0001628280_26_020500.htm`). A meeting on regulatory risk in event contracts and capital return policy would upgrade conviction.

## Risks & inversion
**Primary risk:** **Peak earnings trap** if Q1 2026 rates and equity-index volumes normalize and the market reapplies a lower multiple on transaction revenue.

- **Regulatory pressure** on fees or event-contract products compresses take rates.  
- **Prolonged low volatility** reduces interest-rate and equity-index ADV.  
- **Clearing stress** (member default or collateral disruption) is low probability but would hit reputation and capital return.

**Inversion:** If we are wrong, CME remains a high-quality croupier trading at a full multiple with 5–11% returns, not a broken franchise.

**Lens failure mode (operating):** Thesis fails if handled volume stagnates for several years while competitors gain share in key products.

## Executive summary
CME Group is a toll collector on global derivatives activity: listed futures and options, clearing, and data with minimal principal risk. FY2025 filings confirm **$6,520.6 million** revenue, **$4,229.5 million** operating income, and **$28.7 billion** stockholders' equity; Q1 2026 accelerated to **$1,880.1 million** revenue on strong volumes. At **$252.65** per share (Stooq, 2026-06-03), we expect about **12.01% per year** over 7 years on **$11.40** mid-cycle free cash flow per share (below our portfolio return target for a core add). Asymmetric payoff (Pabrai dhando) stays **partial** because transaction revenue is cyclical. Clearing-member default risk is remote but real; the April 2026 **$7 billion** clearing credit facility amendment is standard infrastructure, not a growth option. We propose **watch** and would revisit near **$210–220** where Lawrence base case approaches our core-return hurdle.

## Risks & inversion
**Primary risk:** Cyclical truck and construction downturn plus sustained Accelera investment could stall owner-earnings growth while **$7.7 billion** of debt limits financial flexibility.

**Additional risks:**

- **Emissions regulation:** Compliance costs and product transitions can compress margins if volumes weaken.
- **China exposure:** Local competition and demand swings affect Engine and Components segments.
- **Accelera execution:** Zero-emissions platforms may require years of spend before meaningful owner cash contribution.
- **Insider selling:** Net sales over the past year weaken insider-alignment signal despite strong operating results.

**Lens failure mode (operating):** If normalized owner earnings fall below **$1.8 billion** for two consecutive years while debt remains above **$7 billion**, the compounder narrative fails and the stock de-rates toward cyclical industrial multiples.

## Risks & inversion
**Primary risk:** AI datacenter capex overshoot plus **$3.2 billion** of debt could leave normalized owner cash stagnant while the equity price embeds sustained hyper-growth.

**Additional risks:**

- **Customer concentration:** Hyperscaler and telecom OEM bargaining power can compress margins.
- **Goodwill impairment:** Lasers unit goodwill **~$3.2 billion**; auditor flagged impairment assessment.
- **Integration / amortization:** Merger-related intangible amortization weighs on reported earnings.
- **Share dilution:** Share count rose from **156M** to **196M** over two years.
- **Cyclical industrial exposure:** Materials and Lasers segments remain cycle-sensitive.

**Lens failure mode (operating):** If normalized owner earnings stay below **$150 million** for two consecutive fiscal years while debt remains above **$3 billion**, the compounder narrative fails and the stock de-rates toward cyclical industrial multiples.

---

## What this business is
Coherent Corp. (NYSE: COHR) designs and manufactures lasers, optical transceivers, engineered materials, and precision photonics systems for communications, industrial, electronics, and instrumentation markets. **[Fact]** FY2025 revenue was **$5.81 billion**, led by the Networking segment at **$3.42 billion** (+49% year over year). **[Fact]** FY2025 operating cash flow was **$634 million** and capital spending was **$441 million**, leaving **$193 million** of normalized owner earnings on a conservative operating-cash-flow-minus-capex basis. **[Fact]** The company carries about **$3.2 billion** of debt and **$2.2 billion** of cash on the March 2026 balance sheet after heavy datacom capacity investment. **[Inference]** Coherent is a capital-intensive photonics compounder riding AI datacenter optical demand while still digesting the II-VI merger, amortization, and preferred-dividend drag.

#### IRR arithmetic (show your work)

How we calculated the annual return (mechanical sync from `valuation.json` calculation proof after contract backfill):

1. Growth from reinvestment = reinvestment rate × incremental return on capital (base: 35% × 18% = 6.3% per year).
2. Year-one owner earnings = starting owner earnings × (1 + growth).
3. Distributable cash each year = owner earnings × (1 − reinvestment rate).
4. Present value of seven years of distributable cash at the discount rate.
5. Terminal value = year-seven owner earnings × terminal multiple; discounted to present.
6. Enterprise value = sum of present values.
7. Equity value = enterprise value + cash − total debt.
8. Value per share = equity value ÷ shares.
9. Annual return at today's price from `valuation_contract.json`.

**Returns statement:** We expect **0.56% per year** at **$124.52**, below our **~15%** hurdle; stance remains **watch** pending human decision.

section: Why the market might be wrong
text:
## Why the market might be wrong
The stock may trade as a levered bet on USDC supply growth and short-term reserve yields while understating how thin normalized owner cash is relative to a **~$12.7 billion** equity market cap at **$80.28**. **[Inference]** FY2025 **operating profit fell to $96.4 million** from **$167 million** in 2024 even as reserve balances grew, because higher operating spend (compliance, distribution, stock compensation, and public-company costs) consumed much of the reserve-yield uplift. **[Inference]** Generalists may treat Circle like a regulated money-market fund wrapper, but shareholders own the franchise margin on float, not the **$75 billion** of segregated reserves. **[Inference]** Conversely, bears may underweight the durability of USDC's compliance-first positioning if U.S. stablecoin legislation clarifies issuer rules. Return here is **earnings power at price**, not a dated catalyst (no HK predictive attribute in base).

---

## Risks & inversion
**Primary risk:** USDC circulation stalls or reverses while the Fed cuts rates, compressing reserve yield before operating costs normalize post-IPO.

- **Competition:** Tether, Paxos, PayPal PYUSD, or bank token offerings take share without equivalent compliance burden.
- **Regulation:** Stablecoin legislation raises reserve, capital, or audit requirements that shrink net spread.
- **Governance / dilution:** Recent IPO and stock-based compensation can dilute per-share owner cash if issuance continues at premium valuations.

**Lens failure mode (operating):** Treating segregated **$75 billion** reserves as equity floor would overstate downside protection; treating Circle as a pure rate proxy would ignore platform optionality and compliance positioning.

**Inversion:** Sustained USDC share gains with platform fees above **10%** of revenue and operating margin recovery would challenge the watch stance.

---

## Executive summary
Base 7-year return **-16.76%** per year (total synthesis) at **$80.28**; stance **watch**. Circle is the regulated issuer behind USDC, earning spread on segregated reserves and building platform fees on top of stablecoin infrastructure. FY2025 showed explosive balance-sheet float growth but compressed operating profit after IPO-era costs; Q1 2026 revenue was **$694 million** (up 20% year-over-year) with **$45 million** operating profit.

At today's price the equity trades near **146 times** normalized owner cash of **$0.55** per share (FY2025 operating profit on ~**158 million** shares), far below our accumulate hurdle. Moat is **stable** (regulated issuer, distribution integrations). Dhando is **partial** (equity cushion, not reserve assets).

## Why the market might be wrong
The stock may trade as a passive infrastructure beneficiary while owner cash is already capital-intensive and levered. **[Inference]** FY2025 operating cash flow was **$5.62 billion** against capital spending of **$2.71 billion**, yet long-term debt on the March 2026 balance sheet was **$16.07 billion** per `10-Q_20260430_rpt20260331_acc0001628280_26_028556.htm`, so equity holders may underweight refinancing and integration risk from serial acquisitions. **[Inference]** Proof-first owner-earnings math at **$99.95** per share (July 2026 price in `valuation.json`) implies mid-single-digit negative annual returns on the automated base bridge even as reported earnings grow, suggesting the market prices reinvestment quality above what the conservative template captures. **[Inference]** Q1 2026 trailing normalized owner earnings (**$2.99 billion**) sit only modestly above the low-case anchor (**$2.91 billion**), while Q3 2025 trailing owner earnings (**$2.61 billion**) were below that anchor, so cyclical seasonality may be misread as steady compounder growth.

## Risks & inversion
**Primary risk:** A sharper construction slowdown coinciding with elevated debt forces equity dilution or curtails buybacks, pulling trailing owner earnings below the low-case **$2.91 billion** anchor.

- Interest expense on **$16+ billion** debt if rates stay higher for longer  
- Integration failure on recent acquisitions (goodwill impairment path)  
- Weather / volume shock in Americas aggregates  
- **Lens failure mode:** treating FY operating cash flow as steady-state owner earnings without TTM normalization

### Moat (Munger)

**Narrow moat (inference):** route density and quarry reserves in Americas materials; not a software-like widening moat. Pricing power is regional and cyclical. Debt-funded scale expansion can destroy moat economics if returns on acquired assets fall below the cost of debt.

### Thesis pillars

1. **Scale in Americas aggregates:** Local logistics and reserve positions support returns in core markets.  
2. **Cash generative through cycle:** Operating cash flow grew to **$5.62B** despite capex rising.  
3. **Capital allocation lever:** Buybacks reduced share count; debt funds M&A (**[HUMAN REVIEW]** on incremental ROIC).

## Executive summary
CRH is a large-scale construction materials compounder with North American weighting, active M&A, and rising capital intensity. FY2025 revenue reached **$37.45 billion** with **$5.62 billion** of operating cash flow; the balance sheet carries **$16.07 billion** of long-term debt against **$3.24 billion** of cash at March 2026. The business is understandable and scaled, but automated proof-first valuation at today’s price embeds generic reinvestment bounds rather than stock-specific underwriting.

At about **$99.95** per share, the legacy contract bridge implies **-7.1%** per year on the base case over seven years (decision-grade component range **$26.05** to **$59.87** to **$128.63** per share). Dhando is **partial** given leverage and cycle exposure. Stance proposal: **watch** pending stock-specific reinvestment proof and independent review of the owner-earnings falsifier draft.

## Executive summary
Salesforce is a subscription software compounder with strong operating cash generation and aggressive share repurchases. FY2026 net income was **$7.46 billion**, operating cash flow **$15.0 billion**, and buybacks **$12.6 billion** per the FY2026 10-K. At **$173.79** per share, the legacy contract bridge implies **7.2%** per year on the automated owner-earnings reinvestment model (migration reference only; contract flags screening-grade assumptions). Proof-first component value spans **$145.56** to **$282.00** to **$559.47** per share (low, base, high). Durable competitive advantage (Munger moat) is **unproven** pending a stock-specific capital bridge. Asymmetric payoff (Pabrai dhando) is **pending**: cash generation is strong but net debt rose materially in FY2026. Stance context **watch** pending human capital authority and independent falsifier review.

### Mental models in plain English

**Switching costs (Munger):** Enterprises embed Salesforce in sales, service, and custom apps. **[Inference]** Migration off the platform is costly in retraining, data migration, and integration rebuilds.

**Critical mass (Lawrence):** The AppExchange ecosystem and ISV partners reinforce the core platform. **[Inference]** Multi-cloud customers (Sales + Service + Data Cloud) raise switching costs versus point solutions.

**Moat trajectory (Munger):** Is competitive advantage widening? **Unproven.** Microsoft bundles CRM with Office and Azure; AI agents may commoditize some workflow layers. **[Inference]** Moat depends on continued innovation in data cloud and Agentforce, not on historical CRM dominance alone.

## Why the market might be wrong
The market prices CrowdStrike as a premium-growth compounder after the July 2024 Falcon content-update incident, yet filing cash economics already support more than $1.3 billion of normalized owner earnings. Investors may overweight GAAP losses and headline churn fears while underweighting operating cash flow that grew 29% compounded over five years and net cash of roughly $4.0 billion against modest long-term debt. If module adoption and net retention stabilize post-incident, owner cash can grow faster than the screening-grade reinvestment template assumes; conversely, if incident-related churn or elevated sales and marketing persist, owner cash could compress toward the low-case bridge typed in the prospective falsifier.

### Moat (Munger)

Competitive advantage appears **unproven** at current prices. Technical leadership and cloud-native architecture helped win share, but Microsoft and other platform vendors bundle competing endpoint tools. Durability depends on module expansion, incident recovery, and maintaining pricing power on renewals. **[HUMAN REVIEW]** on whether net retention has fully normalized post-July 2024.

### Mental models

- **Munger (switching costs):** Falcon agent deployment creates technical stickiness; moat unproven until post-incident retention confirms durability.
- **Munger (incentives):** Heavy stock-based compensation aligns engineers but dilutes owners; read proxy DEF 14A for grant pace.
- **Pabrai (dhando):** Net cash partially bounds downside, but price far exceeds automated owner-cash present value; dhando pending.
- **Stahl (compounder):** Recurring subscription revenue fits software compounder archetype; cycle not applicable.
- **MOI (platform expansion):** Module upsell resembles platform bundling; verify attach rates in MD&A, not marketing alone.

## What this business is
CrowdStrike Holdings sells cloud-native endpoint and identity security software on a subscription model. Customers pay recurring fees for the Falcon platform, which consolidates threat detection, response, and adjacent modules (identity, cloud workload, log management). Revenue reached $4.81 billion in fiscal 2026 (year ended January 31, 2026) per `CRWD/investor-documents/sec-edgar/10-K_20260305_rpt20260131_acc0001535527_26_000010.htm`. The company generates substantial cash from operations ($1.61 billion in fiscal 2026) while reporting a GAAP net loss ($162.5 million) because stock-based compensation and acquisition-related costs remain large relative to reported earnings.

## Why the market might be wrong
**Predictive attribute:** growth narrative versus leverage (headline revenue and backlog versus interest expense, customer concentration, and refinancing risk).

**[Inference]** The market may price CoreWeave as a hyperscaler-compounding cloud franchise because revenue tripled year over year, the stock joined the Nasdaq-100, and NVIDIA invested **$2.0 billion**. **[Fact]** Microsoft alone accounted for roughly **67%** of FY2025 revenue; the top two customers were **77%** in 2024. **[Fact]** Interest expense, net was **$1.2 billion** in FY2025 on **$21.6 billion** of debt at year-end (rising to **$25.1 billion** by Q1 2026). **[Inference]** Investors may underweight the gap between positive operating cash flow (boosted by contract timing and capitalized interest) and equity-level owner cash after debt service, GPU depreciation (**$2.5 billion** FY2025), and continued build-out capex. **[Inference]** The **$60.7 billion** backlog is not per-share net asset value; conversion timing, margin after depreciation, and customer non-performance risk must be modeled explicitly.

## What this business is
CoreWeave, Inc. rents specialized graphics processing unit (GPU) cloud infrastructure to artificial intelligence labs and enterprises. **[Fact]** The company operates AI-native data centers built around NVIDIA GPU clusters (GB200/GB300 systems, InfiniBand networking) and sells compute, storage, and orchestration services under long-term contracts. **[Fact]** FY2025 revenue was **$5.1 billion** (up from **$1.9 billion** in 2024 and **$229 million** in 2023). **[Fact]** At December 31, 2025, remaining performance obligations (contract backlog) totaled **$60.7 billion** versus **$15.1 billion** a year earlier, with a weighted-average contract duration of about **five years**. **[Fact]** The company remains loss-making at the net income line: **$1.2 billion** net loss in FY2025 and **$740 million** in Q1 2026, while reporting **$3.1 billion** of net cash from operating activities in FY2025. **[Fact]** Total debt was **$25.1 billion** at March 31, 2026.

## Executive summary
At **$73.21**, the base case is **6.2% per year** over seven years on normalized starting owner cash of **$1.25 per share** (not raw operating cash flow). CoreWeave is the largest independent GPU cloud renter we cover, with FY2025 revenue **$5.1 billion**, Q1 2026 revenue **$2.1 billion**, and **$60.7 billion** of contracted backlog. Microsoft is **~67%** of revenue; OpenAI and Meta have multi-billion-dollar master agreements. The business generates operating cash flow (**$3.1 billion** FY2025) but loses **$1.2 billion** at net income because interest expense (**$1.2 billion**) and depreciation overwhelm thin operating margins (operating loss **$46 million** FY2025). Total debt is **$25.1 billion** against **$4.8 billion** of equity. Moat is unproven (customer and supplier concentration, hyperscaler competition), dhando is none at this price versus unbounded refinancing and concentration tails, and Marvin proposes **watch** until operating income sustainably covers interest and customer concentration diversifies.

section: Why the market might be wrong
text:
## Why the market might be wrong
A **transitory problem** may dominate: GAAP net income trough (**$7M** FY2025) and Homes.com marketing spend scare generalists away from a sticky CRE subscription core. **[Inference]** The stock is down roughly **54%** over twelve months to **~$33**, while CRE switching costs and data depth remain intact. There is no dated catalyst; residential share gain is optional upside, not required for base CRE economics.

---

### Tier 2 prompts

| Model | Finding |
|-------|---------|
| Critical mass | CoStar Suite embedded in broker workflows; LoopNet liquidity |
| Moat trajectory | CRE stable; residential contested vs Zillow |
| Croupier toll | Value share via subscriptions and marketplace ads, not transaction clearing |

## Executive summary
CoStar combines wide-moat CRE subscriptions with a contested residential land-grab. Normalized free cash flow per share is thin after Homes.com and acquisition amortization, but adj. EBITDA run-rate (~**$644M** annualized from Q1 2026) shows operating earnings power. At **~$33.21** (NASDAQ, ~May 26, 2026), base expected annual return at today's price (Lawrence) is **9.81%** on **$0.95** normalized FCF/share, below the **15%** bar. Durable competitive advantage (Munger moat) is stable in CRE; asymmetric payoff (Pabrai dhando) is partial with residential burn tail risk. We propose **watch** until Homes.com spend moderates or price offers a mid-teens IRR on normalized cash flow.

---

**Inversion:** If we are wrong, CoStar is a fairly priced wide-moat CRE bond with a free residential call option already in the price.

### Mental models in plain English

**Critical mass (Lawrence):** Does the platform need both sides to work? **Yes in CRE**; broker embedding and LoopNet liquidity reinforce each other (`10-K_20260226_rpt20251231_acc0001057352_26_000020.htm`).

**Moat trajectory (Munger):** Is competitive advantage widening? **Stable in CRE, unproven in residential**; Homes.com spend without proven share (`FY2025 MD&A`).

**Croupier toll (Stahl):** Does the company earn fees on activity without principal risk? **Partial**; subscription and ad tolls, not payment clearing (`10-K` segment discussion).

CoStar is a **multi-sided network** (Lawrence bucket): exchanges of listings and data utility, plus a toll-like subscription layer on broker workflows (not a balance-sheet croupier).

#### Synthesis arithmetic (show your work)

1. **Numeric weighted return:** 29%×(-1.0%) + 71%×(14.6%) = **10.01%** per year

section: Why the market might be wrong
text:
## Why the market might be wrong
The market may be paying for **network durability and precision-scheduled railroading efficiency** while underweighting **$18.9 billion of total debt** on the June 2026 balance sheet. A stale 2012 debt tag had implied roughly half that leverage. **[Inference]** At **$50.27**, the stock trades near **7 times** our base proof value per share after refreshing debt from filings, so the market embeds reinvestment returns and terminal economics well above our bounded base case. Insider activity over the past year shows net selling exceeding open-market buys, which weakens a pure "insiders know more" bull case unless sales are largely planned programs.

---

## [HUMAN REVIEW]
- Confirm moat rating after full competitive review versus Norfolk Southern and trucking substitutes.
- Review activist filing history (Mantle Ridge / DFAN14A termination) before stance change.
- Validate reinvestment rate and incremental return on capital against CSX capital spending and ROIC disclosures.

## What this business is
CSX Corporation (NYSE: CSX) operates a Class I freight railroad across 23 eastern states, the District of Columbia, and two Canadian provinces. **[Fact]** FY2025 revenue was **$14.09 billion**, down about **3%** from the prior year per the 2026 proxy summary. **[Fact]** FY2025 operating cash flow was **$4.61 billion** and capital spending was **$2.90 billion**, leaving **$1.71 billion** of normalized owner earnings. **[Inference]** CSX is an eastern U.S. rail compounder: a high fixed-cost network with pricing power on captive lanes, cyclical exposure to industrial and intermodal volumes, and ongoing capital needs to maintain track and equipment.

---

#### IRR arithmetic (show your work)

1. Growth from reinvestment = reinvestment rate × incremental return on capital = 0.35 × 0.18 = **6.3%** per year on owner earnings.
2. Year-one owner earnings = $1.71B × 1.063 = **$1.82B**; distributable cash at 65% payout of earnings = **$1.18B**.
3. Repeat growth on owner earnings for years 2–7; discount distributable cash flows at **10%**.
4. Terminal value = year-seven owner earnings × **18×**; discount to present at year 7.
5. Enterprise value = present value of distributable cash plus terminal present value.
6. Equity value = enterprise value + cash − debt = enterprise value + **$1.01B** − **$18.86B**.
7. Value per share = equity value ÷ **1.85B** shares = **$7.12** (contract base proof).
8. Annual return at today's price = (**$7.12** ÷ **$50.27**)^(1/7) − 1 ≈ **-24.36%** per year.

**Returns statement:** At **$50.27**, the base case implies **-24.36%** per year over seven years on filing-normalized owner earnings and refreshed total debt.

| 6 | Why mispriced? | Inefficiency source? | **Quality / narrative** | Market may pay for duopoly durability and efficiency |

**Dhando (Pabrai):** **Pending.** Franchise economics help versus permanent impairment, but price sits far above proof value and net debt removes cushion.

**Stance proposal:** **watch.** Gate 5 fails; no human capital decision.

**Bear vs base (one sentence):** Bear assumes mid-cycle owner earnings fade and reinvestment returns compress; base holds FY2025 normalized owner cash with bounded reinvestment growth (see proof in `valuation.json`).

The market may be paying for **network durability and precision-scheduled railroading efficiency** while underweighting **$18.9 billion of total debt** on the June 2026 balance sheet. A stale 2012 debt tag had implied roughly half that leverage. **[Inference]** At **$50.27**, the stock trades near **7 times** our base proof value per share after refreshing debt from filings, so the market embeds reinvestment returns and terminal economics well above our bounded base case. Insider activity over the past year shows net selling exceeding open-market buys, which weakens a pure "insiders know more" bull case unless sales are largely planned programs.

## Risks & inversion
**Primary risk:** Medicare Advantage medical-cost trends and pharmacy reimbursement compression persist while **$63.1 billion** of debt limits balance-sheet flexibility.

**Additional risks:**

- **PBM client concentration:** Large employer or government client losses would reduce script volume and rebate economics.
- **Regulatory:** Drug pricing reform, PBM transparency rules, or MA rate cuts could compress margins faster than cost programs offset.
- **Integration execution:** Oak Street and Signify investments must earn returns; failure raises goodwill impairment risk.
- **Leverage:** Rising rates on floating-rate debt increase interest expense against flat owner earnings.

**Lens failure mode (operating):** If normalized owner earnings fall below **$6.0 billion** for two consecutive years while total debt remains above **$60 billion**, the platform compounder narrative fails and the stock de-rates toward sum-of-parts healthcare services multiples.

---

## Executive summary
At **$95.70** (Yahoo close 2026-08-07), our base case annual return is **-4.5%** per year over seven years on filing-normalized owner earnings of **$6.12 per share**, net of **$63.1 billion** of total debt. CVS remains the largest integrated PBM-pharmacy-insurer with **$402 billion** of FY2025 revenue and **$9.8 billion** of cash. Normalized owner earnings of **$7.8 billion** support dividends and reinvestment, but leverage limits financial flexibility if Medicare Advantage margins stay depressed. Component proof base value is **$69 per share**. Moat is **stable** on scale and contract density; dhando is **partial** because business quality does not offset rich price and net debt. Proposed stance: **watch**.

CVS Health Corporation (NYSE: CVS) is an integrated U.S. healthcare platform spanning pharmacy benefit management (Caremark), retail and specialty pharmacy (CVS Pharmacy), health insurance (Aetna), and care-delivery assets including MinuteClinic, Oak Street Health, and Signify Health. **[Fact]** FY2025 consolidated revenue was **$402.1 billion** and operating income was **$4.66 billion**. **[Fact]** FY2025 operating cash flow was **$10.6 billion** and capital spending was **$2.8 billion**, leaving **$7.8 billion** of normalized owner earnings. **[Inference]** CVS monetizes prescription volume, insurance premiums, and medical-cost management through a vertically linked model where PBM formulary control, retail traffic, and Medicare Advantage membership reinforce each other.

section: Why the market might be wrong
text:
## Why the market might be wrong
The market may be pricing **integration synergies and Medicare Advantage recovery** while underweighting **$63.1 billion of debt and lease obligations** on the March 2026 balance sheet and **ongoing reimbursement compression** in both pharmacy and government-sponsored insurance. **[Inference]** At **$95.70**, the stock trades at roughly **1.4 times** our base proof value per share after refreshing debt from filings, implying reinvestment returns and terminal economics above our bounded base case. March 2026 insider open-market purchases by senior executives are a modest positive signal, but net insider activity over the past year still skews heavily to sales.

---

#### Growth mechanism (for assumption ledger)

Base reinvestment model assumes **35%** of owner earnings reinvested at **18%** incremental after-tax return on capital, implying **6.3%** annual owner-earnings growth from reinvestment alone. **[Assumption]** This embeds modest share gains in specialty pharmacy and successful Medicare Advantage margin repair without sizing a separate option terminal.

| 6 | Transitory distribution / legal recovery? | No | n/a | No active litigation recovery in base |

No separate option terminal is sized in base owner cash; care-delivery synergy upside remains **[Assumption]** context unless filings disclose standalone unit economics.

#### IRR arithmetic (show your work)

1. Growth from reinvestment = reinvestment rate × incremental return = **0.35 × 0.18 = 6.3%** per year.
2. Year-1 owner earnings = **$7,807M × 1.063 = $8,299M**; distributable cash = **65% × $8,299M = $5,394M**.
3. Repeat growth for years 2–7; discount each year's distributable cash at **10%**.
4. Present value of seven-year distributable cash ≈ **$26.4 billion**.
5. Year-7 owner earnings ≈ **$11.2 billion**; terminal value = **18 × $11.2B = $201.6B**; present value ≈ **$103.5 billion**.
6. Enterprise value ≈ **$129.9 billion**; plus cash **$9.8B** = **$139.7 billion**; minus debt **$63.1B** = equity **$76.6 billion**.
7. Equity value per share = **$76.6B ÷ 1,276M = $69.21**.
8. Annual return at **$95.70** over 7 years: **($69.21 ÷ $95.70)^(1/7) − 1 ≈ -4.5%** per year.

**Returns statement:** At **$95.70**, the base case annual return is **-4.5%** per year over seven years on filing-normalized owner earnings and refreshed Q1 2026 debt.

## Why the market might be wrong
No dated structural discount or yield-curve setup. **[Inference]** Q1 2026 acceleration (+12% net revenue ex treasury, +18% EBITDA ex treasury) reflects elevated volatility in rates, commodities, and equities; the market may treat that pace as durable. **[Inference]** Declining treasury result (net interest from clearing cash) masks operating strength: total net revenue grew only 9% in Q1 2026 while operating segments grew faster. We normalize on FY2025 owner cash flow, not Q1 2026 peak volumes. **Predictive attribute:** none (franchise earnings at price, not market-structure exclusion).

---

### Mental models in plain English

**Croupier toll (Stahl):** Does the company earn fees on activity without balance-sheet lending risk? **Yes.** Trading, clearing, custody, and index licensing fees (`annual_report_2025.pdf`, business model).

**Volume vs share (Stahl):** Does revenue track handled volume? **Yes.** Q1 2026 net revenue excluding treasury **€1,434M** versus **€1,277M** (+12%); Trading & Clearing net revenue excluding treasury **€688M** versus **€616M** (+12%) (`quarterly_statement_q1_2026.pdf`).

**Fee model resilience (Stahl):** Does recurring revenue cushion cyclicality? **Partially.** Recurring revenue **63%** of total (`annual_report_2025.pdf`, strategy section); treasury result and transaction fees still move with rates and volatility.

**Cycle normalization (Hohn):** Are we using peak trading in the base case? **No.** Starting free cash flow **€12.52** per share from FY2025 operating cash flow minus capital spending, not Q1 2026 annualized net profit **€585 million**.

#### Why these weights (Popper / Deutsch)

Weights are **not** optimized to hit a target return. They encode **epistemic tier**: how independently falsifiable each path is. Template defaults live in `total_synthesis_irr.md`; renormalized shares below sum to 100%.

| Path | Tier | Raw weight | Renormalized | Why this weight | Hard to vary? |
|------|------|------------|--------------|-----------------|---------------|
| Bear scenario (Lawrence) | C (scenario envelope) | 5% | 29% | Downside stress; low weight because bear is a sensitivity, not a competing explanation of  | yes: asymmetric low weight is structural |
| Bull scenario (Lawrence) | C (scenario envelope) | 12% | 71% | Upside stress probe; higher than bear because optionality archetype has skew, but still be | yes |

## Risks & inversion
**Primary risk:** **Treasury result compression** as ECB and global rates fall, masking operating momentum and preventing multiple expansion.

- **Trading volume mean-reversion** after Q1 2026 spike in rates and commodities derivatives.
- **Allfunds integration** (regulatory approvals, synergy timing, financing) and **€1.1 billion** ISS STOXX buyout cash drain in Q1 2026.
- **US regulatory pressure** on ISS proxy-advisory business (Indiana state law challenge noted in Q1 2026 statement).

**Inversion:** If we are wrong, Deutsche Börse remains a high-margin European infrastructure franchise compounding mid-single-digit owner cash with rising dividends, not a broken moat.

**Sources:** `investor-documents/ir-db1/annual_report_2025.pdf`; `investor-documents/ir-db1/quarterly_statement_q1_2026.pdf`

Base **14.48%** per year → **watch**.

## Risks & inversion
**Primary risk:** Persistent inventory shrink, supply-chain disruption, or aggressive price investment by Walmart and Dollar Tree could stall margin recovery while **$4.6 billion** of debt limits balance-sheet flexibility.

**Additional risks:**

- **Labor and turnover:** Store staffing challenges raise wage pressure and hurt customer experience.
- **Regulatory and litigation:** OSHA citations and wage-hour claims elevate compliance costs (10-K risk factors).
- **Store growth returns:** New-store productivity may fall if trade areas overlap or rural markets saturate.
- **Insider selling:** Net sales over the past year weaken insider-alignment signal despite selective open-market buys.

**Lens failure mode (operating):** If normalized owner earnings fall below **$2.0 billion** for two consecutive years while debt stays above **$4.5 billion**, the compounder narrative fails and the stock de-rates toward mid-single-digit retail multiples.

Dollar General Corporation (NYSE: DG) operates more than **20,000** small-box discount stores in **47** U.S. states, focused on rural and small-town communities where larger retailers are scarce. **[Fact]** FY2025 net sales were **$42.7 billion**, up from **$40.6 billion** in FY2024. **[Fact]** The mix is heavily consumables (food, health and beauty, cleaning), with seasonal, apparel, and home categories filling out the basket. **[Fact]** Stores average roughly **7,400 square feet**, use a low-cost build model, and rely on a centralized distribution network. **[Inference]** Dollar General is a high-turn consumables compounder whose economics depend on store density, purchasing scale, and reliable in-stock execution in price-sensitive markets.

Dorchester Minerals, L.P. is a Dallas-based master limited partnership that owns net royalty and mineral interests across U.S. oil and gas basins and distributes essentially all available cash to common unitholders each quarter. **[Fact]** The partnership has no operating employees; revenue is royalty and net profits interest cash from properties operated by third parties. **[Fact]** As of December 31, 2025, **48,255,450** common units were outstanding (`DMLP/investor-documents/sec-edgar/10-K_20260224_rpt20251231_acc0001437749_26_005376.htm`). **[Fact]** FY2025 operating revenues were **$152.8 million**, net income **$57.4 million** (**$1.16** per unit), and declared distributions **$2.775346** per unit (same 10-K). **[Fact]** The partnership agreement requires quarterly distributions equal to **100%** of available cash after reserves (same 10-K, Business section).

Yield-oriented investors may treat Dorchester as a static bond proxy and miss accretive growth from unit-funded mineral acquisitions in 2024-2025. **[Inference]** GAAP net income understates cash distributions because of timing between production and cash receipts. **[Inference]** Screeners focused on earnings yield rather than distribution yield may mis-rank the name versus simpler royalty trusts. **[Inference]** Proof-first component math at base case sums to about **$19.24** per unit of economic value versus a price near **$27**, suggesting the market embeds acreage optionality and mid-cycle commodity assumptions not yet reproduced in filing-locked owner-cash paths.

## What this business is
Dino Polska runs a nationwide chain of mid-sized grocery stores in Poland, mostly in smaller towns and on the edges of larger cities. Shoppers buy everyday food with a heavy fresh mix (meat, produce, bakery) from a standardized format of roughly five thousand products. The company owns much of its logistics: distribution centers replenish stores on a tight cycle so shelves stay stocked without depending on wholesalers. At 31 March 2026 the network had 3,094 stores and twelve distribution centers. Almost all revenue is retail grocery sales in Poland.

## Risks & inversion
**Primary risk:** Discounters and wage inflation compress like-for-like sales and EBITDA margin while the company is still spending heavily on openings, so owner earnings growth stalls and the multiple falls together.

- Single-country Poland exposure (FX, regulation, consumer).
- CapEx intensity: if openings miss returns, accounting FCF stays depressed longer than modeled.
- Governance / liquidity: WSE listing, concentrated ownership, limited English research coverage.

**Lens failure mode (operating):** If growth CapEx is actually maintenance in disguise (replacement of a depreciating network without real white space), starting owner earnings of PLN 2.24 is too high and the base return collapses toward the accounting-FCF path.

Dino is a scale grocery compounder in Poland with owned logistics and a proximity store format aimed at towns larger chains underserve. Dino Polska runs a nationwide chain of mid-sized grocery stores in Poland, mostly in smaller towns and on the edges of larger cities. Shoppers buy everyday food with a heavy fresh mix (meat, produce, bakery) from a standardized format of roughly five thousand products. The company owns much of its logistics: distribution centers replenish stores on a tight cycle so shelves stay stocked without depending on wholesalers. At 31 March 2026 the network had 3,094 stores and twelve distribution centers. Almost all revenue is retail grocery sales in Poland.

The share price fell hard from the 52-week high near PLN 52 toward the high twenties, even while sales kept growing mid-teens and the store count kept rising. Index and narrative money may treat Dino as a crowded Polish retail compounder whose accounting free cash flow looks thin because growth capital spending for new stores and centers consumes cash. The predictive attribute is reinvestment quality: cash from operations still covers growth CapEx, like-for-like sales stayed positive at 4.4%, and white space in several provinces is not exhausted. The inefficiency is confusing growth CapEx with a broken cash engine.

section: Why the market might be wrong
text:
## Why the market might be wrong
The stock may trade as a generic levered healthcare landlord after lab-tenant stress and merger integration noise, while the underlying property cash flows and strategic pivot (Janus spin, lab cluster additions) are more durable than headline GAAP earnings suggest. **[Inference]** FY2025 net income fell sharply even as revenue and operating cash flow grew, so generalists may anchor on **$0.10** basic earnings per share rather than **$1.25 billion** of operating cash flow against a **$10.4 billion** debt stack typical for a large REIT. **[Inference]** Proof-first component math at base case sums to about **−$3.89** per share of filing-locked economic value versus a price near **$22**, suggesting the market prices asset recovery, Janus Living optionality, and refinancing flexibility beyond what the conservative single-component reinvestment model captures today. **[Inference]** Outpatient medical and lab segments (roughly **$796 million** and **$567 million** of segment revenue in FY2025 per 10-K segment tables) may be undervalued relative to senior-housing execution risk that the Janus spin is meant to isolate.

---

#### Thesis pillars

1. **Scale across healthcare property types.** Outpatient medical (**507** properties), lab (**145**), and senior housing (**34**) diversify tenant and reimbursement exposure versus a single-property-type REIT. *(Source: FY2025 10-K segment table.)*
2. **Operating cash flow exceeds reported earnings.** FY2025 operating cash flow grew to **$1.25 billion** while net income fell to **$71 million**, so owner-cash analysis matters more than GAAP EPS for equity holders. *(Source: `filing_facts_2026-08-06.json`.)*
3. **Janus Living simplifies the story.** A planned IPO of the senior housing portfolio (**34 communities / 10,422 units**) could isolate operator complexity and surface value for the remaining lab and outpatient platform. *(Source: FY2025 10-K Item 1.)*
4. **Leverage is the binding constraint.** Long-term debt near **$10.4 billion** against normalized owner earnings of **$357 million** in the mechanical proof makes the equity layer a levered stub until refinancing and spin paths clarify. *(Source: Q1 2026 10-Q; `valuation_fact_ledger.json`.)*

Bear vs base: lab vacancy worsens or refinancing costs rise; bull: Janus IPO clarifies sum-of-the-parts and lab clusters re-rate. Details in `valuation.json` scenarios after refresh.

---

## Executive summary
Healthpeak is a scaled U.S. healthcare REIT spanning outpatient medical, life-science lab, and senior housing assets, with heavy leverage and a planned Janus Living spin to simplify the story. FY2025 results show revenue growth and strong operating cash flow, but reported net income collapsed on non-cash and transaction items. The business is understandable as a levered real estate platform, but the bear case is not tightly bounded at the equity layer given debt maturity and lab-cycle exposure.

At about **$20.81** per share, we expect **6.5%** per year over seven years on the Lawrence owner-cash path (FY2025 operating cash flow **$1.25 billion**, **$1.82** per share, with modest growth and a **12 times** exit multiple **[Assumption]**). Proof-first component economic value base case is **−$3.89** per share pre-floor (**$0** per share after limited-liability floor under explicit zero value policy). Mechanical return math and filing-locked component sum diverge; the levered REIT stub embeds asset recovery and Janus Living optionality beyond conservative proofs. Dhando is **pending**. Stance: **watch**.

The stock may trade as a generic levered healthcare landlord after lab-tenant stress and merger integration noise, while the underlying property cash flows and strategic pivot (Janus spin, lab cluster additions) are more durable than headline GAAP earnings suggest. **[Inference]** FY2025 net income fell sharply even as revenue and operating cash flow grew, so generalists may anchor on **$0.10** basic earnings per share rather than **$1.25 billion** of operating cash flow against a **$10.4 billion** debt stack typical for a large REIT. **[Inference]** Proof-first component math at base case sums to about **−$3.89** per share of filing-locked economic value versus a price near **$22**, suggesting the market prices asset recovery, Janus Living optionality, and refinancing flexibility beyond what the conservative single-component reinvestment model captures today. **[Inference]** Outpatient medical and lab segments (roughly **$796 million** and **$567 million** of segment revenue in FY2025 per 10-K segment tables) may be undervalued relative to senior-housing execution risk that the Janus spin is meant to isolate.

## Why the market might be wrong
The market may treat Deterra as a single-commodity iron ore yield stock and miss the option stack in Thacker Pass lithium (first production late 2027) and the gold offtake book acquired via Trident. **[Inference]** FY2025 gold offtake net revenue margin was **A$21.5 million** on record gold prices, diversifying cash away from MAC iron ore alone. **[Inference]** The 1H25 interim dividend cut to **9 cents** (from **14.89 cents** in 1H24) may anchor yield screens on a trough payout rather than the **75% of NPAT** policy confirmed at FY25. Index and domestic yield buyers may underweight ASX royalty structures relative to US trust equivalents (MSB, SJT).

Deterra Royalties is an ASX-listed passive royalty company that receives cash from mining operators without operating mines or bearing production capital spending. **[Fact]** The cornerstone asset is a **1.232%** gross revenue royalty over BHP's Mining Area C (MAC) iron ore hub in Western Australia, plus **A$1 million** capacity payments per million dry metric tonnes of annual production increase (`DRR.AX/investor-documents/official-reports/250325-1HY25-Deterra-Royalties-Financial-Results-Declaration.pdf`). **[Fact]** FY2025 revenue was **A$263.4 million** (+10%); underlying EBITDA **A$250 million** (+10%); net profit after tax **A$155.7 million**; total dividends **22 cents** per share fully franked (`DRR.AX/investor-documents/asx-announcements/2931000.pdf`). **[Fact]** At 31 December 2024, net assets were **19.1 cents** per share while net tangible assets were **(42.1) cents** per share because royalty intangibles are excluded from NTA (same half-year report). **[Fact]** Net debt at 30 June 2025 was **A$271 million** with **A$205 million** undrawn on **A$500 million** credit facilities (FY25 results presentation).

The market may treat Deterra as a single-commodity iron ore yield stock and miss the option stack in Thacker Pass lithium (first production late 2027) and the gold offtake book acquired via Trident. **[Inference]** FY2025 gold offtake net revenue margin was **A$21.5 million** on record gold prices, diversifying cash away from MAC iron ore alone. **[Inference]** The 1H25 interim dividend cut to **9 cents** (from **14.89 cents** in 1H24) may anchor yield screens on a trough payout rather than the **75% of NPAT** policy confirmed at FY25. Index and domestic yield buyers may underweight ASX royalty structures relative to US trust equivalents (MSB, SJT).

**Primary risk:** Medicare and Medicare Advantage reimbursement changes plus **$10.5 billion** of debt could compress owner cash faster than treatment volumes grow.

**Additional risks:**

- **Payer mix:** Commercial rate pressure or MA coding changes can move margins quickly.
- **Labor and center costs:** Nurse and technician wages affect center-level profitability.
- **Leverage and refinancing:** Higher rates or tighter covenants limit flexibility if owner cash weakens.
- **Policy / regulatory:** CMS rate-setting and litigation over payment models remain ongoing overhangs.

**Lens failure mode (operating):** If normalized owner earnings fall below **$1.0 billion** for two consecutive years while debt remains above **$10 billion**, the compounder narrative fails and the stock de-rates toward leveraged healthcare operator multiples.

4. Enterprise value plus cash **$726M**, minus debt **$10,514M**, equals equity value **~$14.0B**; divide by **64.2M** shares for **$218** value per share (contract base).

## Risks & inversion
**Primary risk:** **Peak earnings trap** if Q1 2026 volatility normalizes and the market reapplies a lower multiple on transaction revenue.

- **Regulatory fee pressure** in EU equities or clearing could compress take rates.
- **Competitive share loss** to MTFs or off-exchange venues despite **64%** cash equity share.
- **M&A integration** (Admincontrol, Athens) could distract capital or miss synergy targets.
- **Governance friction** among reference shareholders on large deals (historical LSE bid overhang pattern in TCI letters).

**Lens failure mode (operating):** If moat erodes via share loss faster than handled volume grows, cyclical revenue dominates and terminal multiple compresses toward bear case.

## What this business is
Euronext N.V. is the leading pan-European market infrastructure group: regulated equity, fixed-income, and derivatives venues, central counterparty clearing, securities services, market data, and primary listings across Amsterdam, Paris, Brussels, Lisbon, Milan, Oslo, Dublin, and Athens. **[Fact]** FY2025 underlying revenue and income was **€1,823.2 million** (+12.1% versus 2024), adjusted EBITDA reached about **€1.1 billion**, and free cash flow was **€682.3 million** (`investor-documents/ir-euronext/urd_2025.pdf`, §5.2.4). **[Fact]** Q1 2026 underlying revenue and income was **€528.5 million** (+15.3% versus Q1 2025), with adjusted EBITDA **€343.2 million** and margin **64.9%** (`investor-documents/ir-euronext/q1_2026_press_release.pdf`). The company earns toll-like fees on trading, clearing, listing, custody, and data subscriptions with minimal principal risk on core operations (Stahl croupier).

## Executive summary
Euronext is a Stahl croupier at **€145.70** per share: we expect about **10.29% per year** over 7 years on mid-cycle FY2025 owner cash, below our about-fifteen-percent target. Lawrence bear and bull scenarios span **5.2%** to **12.7%** per year. FY2025 filings confirm **€1,823 million** underlying revenue, **€682 million** free cash flow, and **€7.27** adjusted earnings per share; Q1 2026 accelerated to **€528.5 million** revenue (+15.3%) with **56%** non-volume-related mix covering **159%** of underlying operating expenses. Management is executing the **Innovate for Growth 2027** plan (clearing expansion, data and Athens integration, active buybacks). Dhando is **partial** because volume-linked revenue remains cyclical despite a growing recurring stack. We propose **watch** and would revisit nearer **€105–115** for a **15%** base annual return band.

## What this business is
iShares Ethereum Trust ETF (NASDAQ: **ETHA**) is a passive Delaware statutory trust sponsored by iShares Delaware Trust Sponsor LLC (BlackRock affiliate). **[Fact]** The trust holds **ether and cash only** and seeks to reflect the price of ether **before** trust expenses and liabilities. **[Fact]** Shares trade on NASDAQ; authorized participants create and redeem **40,000-share baskets** against cash and ether via prime execution and custodial arrangements. **[Fact]** The trust seeded on **May 21, 2024** and began operations on **June 24, 2024** when seed proceeds purchased roughly **3,031 ether**. **[Fact]** At **March 31, 2026**, net asset value was **$6.38 billion** on **401.88 million** shares (about **$15.87** net asset value per share), down from **$10.30 billion** and **458.72 million** shares at **December 31, 2025**, after ether fell **29%** in the quarter and redemptions exceeded creations.

---

## Risks & inversion
**Primary risk:** Ether price declines materially and stays depressed; the trust cannot “reinvest” its way out because it is passive.

**Inversion:** If ether re-rates higher on institutional adoption, ETHA captures beta minus fees with daily liquidity versus self-custody.

- **Regulatory:** SEC and court uncertainty on ether security status (10-K risk factors).
- **Protocol:** Ethereum network changes could affect ether value (10-K risk factors).
- **Operational:** Custody, prime execution agent, trade credit facility failures (10-K / 10-Q).
- **Market structure:** Premium/discount persistence; AP withdrawal; thin trading (10-K).
- **Concentration:** Large ether holders moving price (10-K digital asset market risks).

**Lens failure mode:** Applying **owner-earnings reinvestment** math to a **zero free cash flow** wrapper, or ignoring **fee compounding** and **NAV basis** at purchase.

#### IRR arithmetic (show your work)

**Base case** (dated payoff on projected net asset value per share).

1. Starting net asset value per share **$15.87** (10-Q Mar 31, 2026).
2. Grow with **8% per year** ether path for seven years: $15.87 × 1.08^7 ≈ **$27.19**.
3. Apply cumulative **0.25% per year** fee drag: × 0.9975^7 ≈ **0.983** → projected net asset value ≈ **$26.70** per share.
4. Entry price **$20.37** (Yahoo 2026-10-01).
5. Total return factor = 26.70 ÷ 20.37 ≈ **1.311** over seven years.
6. Annual return = 1.311^(1/7) − 1 ≈ **3.9% per year**.

**Returns statement:** Base case annual return **3.9%** at price **$20.37** (ether spot grows eight percent per year in the model; sponsor fee 0.25% per year on net asset value).

**Upside / downside from price:** Buying at filed net asset value (**$15.87**) with the same ether path raises the annual return to roughly **9% per year**. Buying above net asset value, as today, compresses the return even if ether performs well.

## Why the market might be wrong
**Predictive attribute:** **wrapper tracking basis** (exchange-traded share price versus net asset value, fee drag, and after-hours ether moves versus NASDAQ session).

**[Inference]** Investors may treat ETHA as a generic “compounder” equity when the filing describes a **non-managed** vehicle with **no distributions** and a single recurring cost: the **0.25%** sponsor fee (partially waived at launch). **[Fact]** Shares **may trade at, above, or below** net asset value; non-concurrent ether market hours versus NASDAQ can widen discounts or premiums. **[Inference]** After the **July 23, 2025** fee-waiver expiry, total expense drag on assets **increased** for the first **$2.5 billion** of scale, which easy-flow inflows during 2025 may have masked. **[Inference]** Q1 2026 **net redemptions** (131.5 million shares redeemed versus 74.7 million created) may signal allocator rotation among spot ether products rather than a change in ether fundamentals alone.
