section: Why the market might be wrong
text:
## Why the market might be wrong
The market may treat Evolve as a thinly traded CSE micro-cap and miss the inflection from one cash-flowing royalty at year-start toward four by year-end 2026. **[Inference]** At C$2.80 the stock trades near a 34% discount to the roughly C$4.26 per share net asset value implied by peer price-to-NAV multiples in the February 2026 corporate presentation, while Royalty King screen work flagged Evolve as the only junior royalty name near 0.75 times NAV versus peers at 1.0 to 1.7 times **[PENDING APPROVAL]**. **[Inference]** CSE listing friction, small float, and no dividend yet may exclude yield-screen buyers even as Uis tin and Highland Valley copper payments accelerate with elevated commodity prices.

---

|---|----------|--------|-----------|----------|

| 3 | In-business loss segment? | No | n/a | Royalty-only G&A model |
| 4 | Backlog / contracted revenue not in FCF? | Yes | embedded_in_segment | McIlvenna Bay Q3 2026; Copper Mountain post-carveout |
| 5 | Private stakes below fair value? | Partial | milestone_nav | C$9M cash plus securities and private debenture |
| 6 | Transitory distribution / legal recovery? | No | n/a | No dividend program |
| 7 | Embedded option in revenue? | Yes | embedded_in_segment | HVC and Uis in YTD C$2.70M |

### Five-question gate

| # | Gate | Answer |
|---|------|--------|
| 1 | Understand? | Yes: passive royalties on copper/tin/lithium |
| 2 | Durable cash flow? | Partial: producing base growing; commodity-linked |
| 3 | Bounded bear? | Partial: no debt; bear is multiple plus flat royalties |
| 4 | Aligned management? | Yes: Nomad founders; significant insider ownership per presentation **[Assumption]** pending FY2025 AIF |
| 5 | Cheap vs normalized? | Partial: ~34% NAV discount; Lawrence IRR below 15% bar |
| 6 | Why mispriced? | CSE micro-cap; no dividend; ramp not in screens yet |

**Dhando (Pabrai):** **partial**. Downside bounded by royalty-only model and no debt, but commodity and junior-multiple risk prevent full dhando.

**Stance proposal:** **hold** (synthesis **14.9%** marginal vs 15% bar; optionality NAV floor passes per `optionality_gate`).

**Bear vs bull (one line):** Bear assumes flat owner cash and 12 times exit multiple; bull adds four-royalty ramp, Sal de Los Angeles option, and peer multiple re-rate toward 1.0 times NAV.

## Risks & inversion
**Primary risk:** Commodity price downturn compresses royalty receipts and junior multiples simultaneously, leaving the NAV discount in place.

- Teck's Highland Valley permitted mine life historically cited to 2027 before MLE; extension execution risk remains
- Uis acquisition consumed US$22.5M cash plus 4.2M shares; integration and tin price sensitivity
- Copper Mountain payments deferred until US$10M pre-tax exclusion clears (US$6.7M paid to date)
- CSE liquidity and short operating history limit institutional ownership
- Argentina lithium (LAA) construction timing tied to Tibet Summit capital allocation and lithium prices

**Lens failure mode (asset / optionality):** If development royalties (McIlvenna, Copper Mountain, LAA) slip beyond 2027, the investment becomes a two-asset micro-royalty at a premium to run-rate cash, and the NAV discount thesis fails.

---

## Executive summary
Evolve is a copper-and-tin royalty vehicle built by the former Nomad team, now ramping from one producing royalty to four in 2026 while trading at a material discount to peer NAV multiples. At **C$2.80** (2026-06-11), we expect **14.9%** per year on the total synthesis case (Lawrence base **13.8%**; bear **4.2%**, bull **20.5%**). Year-to-date royalty receipts of **C$2.70 million** and the Uis acquisition add immediate cash flow; McIlvenna Bay and Copper Mountain provide the next legs. Moat is **unproven** on a four-month public track record but operator quality (Teck, Hudbay, Eldorado, Andrada) is strong. Dhando is **partial**: no debt and royalty-only risk, but commodity cyclicality and junior multiple risk cap the bear case. We propose **hold**: synthesis **14.9%** is marginal versus our 15% accumulate bar, but the **34% NAV discount** passes the optionality floor (peer re-rate path).

## Business & moat

Fair Isaac is a toll collector on credit decisions, not a lender. The annual report describes two segments. Scores are the toll. Software is the set of tools lenders use around the decision. In fiscal 2025, business-to-business scores were $949 million, 81% of Scores, and direct-to-consumer scores were $220 million. Operating income was 88% of Scores revenue, the same as the year before. Software revenue was $822 million and grew 3%, while Software operating income fell $9.8 million. Nine months into fiscal 2026, Scores were already $1.24 billion, more than the entire prior year, and total company revenue was $1.88 billion. Quarter revenue was $674 million. Operating income for the nine months was $999 million. Interest expense, net, for those nine months was $146 million, up from $94 million. The quarterly report ties the higher interest to a higher average debt balance: the $1.5 billion of notes issued in May 2025, $1.0 billion of 6.25% notes issued in March 2026, a $1.5 billion term loan borrowed in full on June 5, 2026, and a higher balance on the revolving credit line. The June term loan matures May 15, 2028, and the company used it to fund an accelerated share repurchase. Long-term debt at June 30, 2026 was $5.28 billion, against $2.66 billion at September 30, 2025.

The distribution fact matters more after this week than it did in July. In the June quarter, agreements with the three bureaus were 63% of revenue, up from 54% a year earlier, and up from 51% for all of fiscal 2025. Those same three bureaus own VantageScore. They are the shelf and the rival.

The annual report already names the two risks that arrived as news. One is regulatory attention to mortgage closing costs, which "may affect our ability to implement price changes for FICO Scores used in mortgage originations." The other is the Federal Housing Finance Agency's process for approving score models at Fannie Mae and Freddie Mac. The September news is that process being used. Early in September, lenders delivering loans to the two mortgage giants could use Classic FICO or VantageScore 4.0, but VantageScore was marked down 20 points so it would not look stronger than it is. On September 28, Director Bill Pulte said the two grids become one, and that 20-point mark-down is gone. A borrower scored at 780 on either model can reach the same top pricing band. Classic FICO remains an option. It is still required when a human underwrites the loan. FICO's newer 10T score is not approved for delivery to Fannie and Freddie. The housing agency that insures other loans, FHA, plans to start using 10T in January 2027.

Rocket Mortgage said it will be the first lender to prefer VantageScore 4.0 on eligible loans, after running both models on 1.4 million credit reports. Borrowers who saved money saved about $1,600 at closing, on Rocket's account. United Wholesale Mortgage has said about a quarter of its borrowers score better on VantageScore, and that share might reach 40% by the end of September. - The filing does not isolate mortgage origination scores. Until it does, any percent of profit "at risk" is a guess and is kept out of the base path.

#### Thematic context

The context file for September 29 marks a wider high-yield credit spread. That is a backdrop for mortgage volume, which is the other half of score fees. It is not an input to the return below. The event that changes the story is the pricing grid, not the spread.

Moat. The advantage on mortgage origination scores narrowed this week from "the score the mortgage giants require" to "one of two scores, and the expensive one." The advantage on everything else is intact until someone shows volume leaving. A moat that depends on a single regulator's grid is a franchise with a political lease, not a law of nature.

## What this business is

Fair Isaac sells a credit score and the software that uses scores in lending decisions. The three national credit bureaus, Experian, TransUnion, and Equifax, run the formula on their files and pay Fair Isaac a fee for each score. A smaller direct-to-consumer business sells scores at myFICO.com. The software segment covers fraud, origination, account management, and a subscription platform. In the year ended September 30, 2025, Scores were $1.17 billion and Software was $822 million.

### Mental models

This is a standard that became a habit, then a requirement, then a price. Requirements can be rewritten. Habits change more slowly. The bureaus have a reason to hurry the change, because they keep more of a VantageScore fee than of a FICO fee. Lenders have a reason to hurry if the score lets them offer a cheaper rate. Investors who assume the unit price only goes up are using last year's mechanism.

## Executive summary

On September 29, 2026, Fair Isaac closed at $617.87, down 26.5% on the day and 51% below the July 20 close in the valuation file. Fannie Mae and Freddie Mac will price Classic FICO and VantageScore 4.0 on one mortgage grid, and they dropped a 20-point penalty on the rival score. Rocket Mortgage said it will prefer VantageScore. The last quarter did not show a volume collapse. Scores revenue was $459 million, up from $324 million, and management tied the business-to-business increase to a higher mortgage unit price. Long-term debt was already $5.28 billion at June 30, including a $1.5 billion term loan used to buy back stock. If free cash flow grows 4% a year for five years and 3% after that, and the business is worth 16 times year-ten cash flow, the return is about **9%** per year. That prices a toll that can no longer be raised at will. A real cut in mortgage score fees would leave a much smaller return. Stance stays watch.

## Risks & inversion

**Primary risk:** Mortgage origination score prices move toward the rival's price, and the bureaus prefer the score they own. text:
## Why the market might be wrong

The September 29 selloff prices a break in mortgage score pricing power. That reading fits the last quarterly report, which said business-to-business score growth came mainly from a higher mortgage unit price. It does not fit a claim that the whole company just lost its customers. Classic FICO is still allowed at Fannie Mae and Freddie Mac, and it is still required when a loan is underwritten by hand. The market can be wrong in either direction: too fearful if lenders keep paying up for the familiar score, or not fearful enough if the bureaus, who own the cheaper rival and distribute FICO, steer volume away.

## [PROPOSED MEMORY]

- FICO mortgage score growth was a unit-price story in the June 2026 quarter, and the September 29 single pricing grid attacks that mechanism rather than reported volume.

#### IRR arithmetic (show your work)

1. Starting free cash flow per share is $36.06.
2. After five years at 4%, free cash flow per share is $43.87.
3. After five more years at 3%, year-ten free cash flow per share is $50.86.
4. Sixteen times that cash flow is an exit value of $814 per share.
5. The buyer also receives each year's cash flow along the way, starting from $36 and ending near $51.
6. The single rate that turns a $617.87 purchase into those ten cash flows plus the $814 exit is 9% per year.

**Upside / downside from price:** The same path was about a zero return at the July 20 price of $1,263.83, and about 5% per year at the September 28 close of $840.89. The selloff did the work of lowering the price. It did not raise the cash flow. If cash flow stays at $36 per share and the exit is only 12 times, the return is about 3% per year.

**Returns statement:** About **9%** per year at the September 29 close, if cash flow grows modestly and mortgage score fees do not reset downward.

Fair Isaac sells a credit score and the software that uses scores in lending decisions. The three national credit bureaus, Experian, TransUnion, and Equifax, run the formula on their files and pay Fair Isaac a fee for each score. A smaller direct-to-consumer business sells scores at myFICO.com. The software segment covers fraud, origination, account management, and a subscription platform. In the year ended September 30, 2025, Scores were $1.17 billion and Software was $822 million.

The September 29 selloff prices a break in mortgage score pricing power. That reading fits the last quarterly report, which said business-to-business score growth came mainly from a higher mortgage unit price. It does not fit a claim that the whole company just lost its customers. Classic FICO is still allowed at Fannie Mae and Freddie Mac, and it is still required when a loan is underwritten by hand. The market can be wrong in either direction: too fearful if lenders keep paying up for the familiar score, or not fearful enough if the bureaus, who own the cheaper rival and distribute FICO, steer volume away.

## What this business is
Firefly Aerospace Inc. is a Nasdaq-listed U.S. space and defense technology company selling end-to-end mission solutions: small and medium launch (Alpha and Eclipse rockets), spacecraft (Blue Ghost lunar lander and Elytra orbital vehicles), and defense software and sensing (SciTec, acquired October 2025). **[Fact]** Customers are primarily U.S. national security agencies, NASA, and prime contractors. **[Fact]** FY2025 revenue was **$159.9 million** (+163% versus **$60.8 million** in FY2024). **[Fact]** Q1 2026 revenue was **$80.9 million** (+45% year-over-year versus **$55.9 million**). **[Fact]** The company had **1,409 employees** at December 31, 2025, including **436** with active national security clearances (10-K Item 1).

## Why the market might be wrong
The market may treat Franco-Nevada as a passive gold beta at a peak multiple and underweight the portfolio option stack. **[Inference]** Record FY2025-Q1 2026 cash flows embed elevated gold, silver, and (in Q2 outlook) oil prices; a quality premium may compress if commodities normalize. **[Inference]** Cobre Panamá restart, recent acquisitions (Cascabel buy-back, Victoria Gold portfolio, Bullabulling), and operator exploration spend on the royalty book are not fully in 2026 GEO guidance. **[Inference]** Unlike operating miners, Franco-Nevada benefits from higher oil prices without proportionate cost inflation (CEO Q1 2026 remarks).

The market may treat Fermi either as a failed tenant story after the September 2025 non-binding letter of intent expired, or as a speculative nuclear developer, when the filing picture is closer to a pre-lease infrastructure REIT with **$1.4 billion** of capitalized project assets and permitted gas capacity already on the balance sheet. **[Inference]** Governance noise (CEO termination, proxy contest, securities litigation) can obscure that vertical construction is explicitly gated on a definitive tenant lease, not on speculative science-project timelines. **[Inference]** If hyperscaler power scarcity persists, the predictive attribute is a **dated catalyst**: first powered-shell commercial operations targeted for **2027** once a binding lease triggers vertical build.

FRMO Corporation is a Delaware holding company affiliated with Horizon Kinetics. It does not run an operating business. **[Fact]** It owns concentrated stakes in investment partnerships, exchange infrastructure (Miami International Holdings), Horizon Kinetics Holding Corp., and smaller fund and digital-asset positions. Revenue to shareholders comes from fair-value marks on those investments, advisory royalty interests, and fund economics, not from product sales. **[Fact]** As of February 28, 2026, total assets were $919.5 million and FRMO-attributable stockholders' equity was $376.7 million, about $8.55 per share. **[Fact]** Roughly 82% of FRMO's equity sits in a single consolidated investment position ("Investment A"). The stock trades OTC with thin liquidity.

The market prices FRMO like a volatile mark-to-market fund, not like a sum of parts. **[Inference]** OTC trading, fair-value earnings swings (Q3 FY2026 diluted EPS $1.89 vs a $0.54 loss a year earlier), and concentration in one line item push generalist investors away. **[Inference]** Private stakes (MIH post-IPO, HKHC, Winland, catalyst names) are likely carried below economic value in GAAP marks. Horizon Kinetics calls this a **dormant asset** case: value sits in subsidiaries and listing events, not in trailing GAAP earnings. There is no clean equity yield curve with one dated payoff; return depends on a catalyst stack over several years.

## Risks & inversion
**Primary risk:** Paying **~3 times** book and **~4 times** liquid assets for a cyclical crop-share and royalty stream while dividends (**$40/sh**) consume most normalized owner cash (**~$53/sh**), leaving little retained capital if farm rental and oil royalties stay at FY2024 trough levels.

- **Inversion:** A return to FY2022 revenue (**$8.9M**) plus securities gains could support dividends and re-rate equity toward higher book-plus-land marks without new debt.
- Postretirement health obligation (**$1.28M**, unfunded) grows with actuarial losses and healthcare inflation (Note 7).
- Southwest Kansas water regulation and drought risk sit in "water issues" expenses (**$1.1M** G&A FY2024).
- OTC illiquidity may prevent exit at quoted prices; option plan uses **~$1,284** strike as best filing anchor for value.
- Investment portfolio marks (**$364K** unrealized gain FY2024) can reverse and swing reported earnings.

**Lens failure mode (asset payoff):** If supplemental acreage shows modest acreage or heavy irrigation capital needs, the land remark in our overlay is too high and the name is purely a low-growth dividend bond priced for yield, not NAV.

## What this business is
The Garden City Company is a closely held farmland and royalty company headquartered in Garden City, Kansas, with a secondary office in Colorado Springs. **[Fact]** The company owns farmland in southwest Kansas that it leases to tenant farmers on an annual **crop-share** basis: revenue is recognized when crops are harvested and inventoried, and grain inventory on the balance sheet represents the company's share of unsold crops. **[Fact]** It also collects **oil and gas royalties** from wells operated by third parties on its land. **[Fact]** As of December 31, 2024, **34,865** shares were outstanding; stockholders' equity was **$14.2 million** (**~$407** per share). **[Fact]** The company carries **no bank debt**, invests surplus cash in U.S. Treasury and equity securities (**$8.1 million** fair value at year-end 2024), and pays a large annual cash dividend (**$40** per share in 2024, **$45** in 2023). **[Fact]** Leadership includes President and CEO R. ## Why the market might be wrong
The market may treat GCCO as an illiquid family dividend stub, either ignoring the **embedded liquid-asset and farmland bundle** or overpaying after a multi-year move above book value. **[Fact]** At an indicative **~$1,284** per share (December 2024 stock option exercise price), the stock trades roughly **3.2 times** December 2024 GAAP book (**~$407** per share) and about **4 times** mark-to-market liquid assets (cash, securities, and grain inventory, **~$317** per share combined). **[Inference]** Predictive attribute: **family-controlled farmland OTC** plus **market structure discount** (no exchange listing, thin volume, dividend screens only). **[Inference]** Land and water rights are carried at **historical cost** (**$2.93 million** on the balance sheet); supplemental acreage schedules in older PDFs were not text-extracted in this workspace, so economic farmland value may exceed GAAP but is **[Assumption]** until verified. **[Inference]** FY2024 farm rental and oil/gas revenues fell versus 2023 on crop and commodity prices, so trailing earnings understate mid-cycle cash generation but also show cyclical risk.

---

## Executive summary
Garden City is a debt-free Kansas farmland and royalty vehicle that pays most of its operating cash back as dividends. FY2024 normalized owner cash (operating cash flow minus capital spending) was about **$53** per share on **$6.4 million** of revenue, down from stronger 2022 crop and oil prices. At **~$1,284** per share **[Assumption]**, our base case annual return is **-0.9%** per year (total synthesis on filing-based owner cash with modest growth and a **14 times** year-10 cash-flow exit multiple; Lawrence filing path **-1.4%**). Liquid assets near **$317** per share and GAAP book **~$407** per share cap downside versus a zero, but the quote sits well above both, so **floor_pass** is false. Dhando is **partial**: no debt and tangible assets help, but premium pricing and family control limit minority upside. We propose **watch** until a verified live quote, FY2025 OCR, or supplemental acreage marks justify accumulate.

Thayer Tutt, Jr. and a board chaired by William J. Hybl; the stock trades OTC Pink (GCCO) with audited GAAP financials posted via OTC Markets.

The market may treat GCCO as an illiquid family dividend stub, either ignoring the **embedded liquid-asset and farmland bundle** or overpaying after a multi-year move above book value. **[Fact]** At an indicative **~$1,284** per share (December 2024 stock option exercise price), the stock trades roughly **3.2 times** December 2024 GAAP book (**~$407** per share) and about **4 times** mark-to-market liquid assets (cash, securities, and grain inventory, **~$317** per share combined). **[Inference]** Predictive attribute: **family-controlled farmland OTC** plus **market structure discount** (no exchange listing, thin volume, dividend screens only). **[Inference]** Land and water rights are carried at **historical cost** (**$2.93 million** on the balance sheet); supplemental acreage schedules in older PDFs were not text-extracted in this workspace, so economic farmland value may exceed GAAP but is **[Assumption]** until verified. **[Inference]** FY2024 farm rental and oil/gas revenues fell versus 2023 on crop and commodity prices, so trailing earnings understate mid-cycle cash generation but also show cyclical risk.

## Executive summary

Gold Reserve Ltd. is a Bermuda judgment-collection vehicle pursuing ICSID and CITGO-related recoveries plus a long-dated Arb II option. It is not an operating gold miner. Local folders hold Delaware sale orders, Lisbon recognition, Arb II pleadings, and a PFIC notice, but not the latest SEDAR financial statements. At **$4.56** per share the market capitalizes substantial recovery expectations versus a soft cash floor near **$0.68** per share. Proof-first component math sums to about **$5.68** per share of economic value today. The stance-gate base case earns **11.3%** if a **$7** per share risked payoff arrives in about four years, below our fifteen percent target after process and ranking risk. Dhando is partial. Stance: **watch** pending SEDAR verification and Amber closing.

Gold Reserve Ltd. is a Bermuda company (continued from Alberta in September 2024) that no longer operates a mine. **[Fact]** Its economic identity is a **judgment-and-claim vehicle**: collect unpaid amounts under a 2014 ICSID award and 2016 Venezuela settlement, participate as a creditor/bidder in the Delaware forced sale of PDV Holding (CITGO’s parent stack), and prosecute a 2025 arbitration over revoked Siembra Minera mining rights. **[Fact]** Shares trade as **GDRZF** (OTCQX) and **GRZ.V** (TSXV). **[Fact]** The company deregistered from the SEC on 30 January 2025, so U.S. EDGAR is no longer the primary reporting channel. **[Fact]**

## Why the market might be wrong
The stock may trade like a levered crypto proxy while understating the recurring fee and infrastructure franchise. **[Inference]** FY2025 **Adjusted EBITDA was only $33.7 million** (down from **$715.4 million** in 2024) because treasury marks and trading volatility dominated GAAP earnings, not because fee lines collapsed: **fees rose 54%** to **$159 million** and blockchain rewards grew to **$220 million**. **[Inference]** The **Helios** data-center pivot (CoreWeave lease, **133 MW** of critical IT load targeted by mid-2026) is priced as optionality with **zero Data Center segment revenue** in FY2025. **[Inference]** Complexity (dual share classes, digital-asset balance sheet, mark-to-market earnings) keeps generalist investors away, so the market may overweight trailing losses and underweight institutional wallet share.

---

### What (Stahl + Lawrence bucket)

| Field | Value | Evidence |
|-------|-------|----------|
| Archetype | platform | Trading + asset management + infra on shared client stack |
| Cycle | trough | FY2025 marks-driven loss after 2024 peak |

There is **no clear dated mispricing signal** (Horizon Kinetics predictive attribute: **none**). **[Inference]** At today's price, the stock prices Cloud AI optionality and Search resilience together; it is not a holdco-discount or dormant-asset story. **[Inference]** A single consolidated free cash flow growth rate hides **divergent segment economics**: Services throws off most cash today while Cloud and Alphabet-level spend absorb the 2026 capex guide. **[Inference]** Lawrence ten-year math on **FY2025 free cash flow per share ($5.85)** may understate medium-term earnings if capital spending normalizes after 2027; the segment build makes that tension explicit. **[Inference]** GOOG typically trades at a small discount to GOOGL (no voting rights); that spread is not a separate business thesis but a governance preference for owners who do not need votes.

section: Why the market might be wrong
text:
## Why the market might be wrong
No dated structural discount or equity yield curve setup at today's price. **[Inference]** Polish capital-market recovery and record Main Market turnover in Q1 2025 may justify a quality premium, but at PLN 83.6 the stock prices much of that recovery already. **[Inference]** Foreign client revenue (37.1% of Q1 sales) and commodity gas spot growth are under-modeled in simple domestic-equity narratives, yet they do not clear our 15% annual return hurdle at spot.

---

## Risks & inversion
**Primary risk:** Equity turnover mean-reversion after the 2024 and 2025 recovery; Polish political or regulatory shifts affecting market structure or PFSA fees.

**Inversion checklist:**
- If Main Market daily turnover falls back below PLN 1.2 billion for two consecutive quarters, growth assumptions fail.
- If State Treasury pursues policy that caps fee yields or diverts cash to non-shareholder goals, moat and alignment weaken.
- If intangible IT capex stays above PLN 40 million per year without revenue follow-through, owner cash conversion stays below earnings.

**Lens failure mode:** Operating lens assumes normalized fee volume persists; a prolonged domestic equity bear market breaks the base case without a dated recovery path.

---

### Five-question gate

| # | Gate | Answer |
|---|------|--------|
| 1 | Understand? | Yes. Financial + commodity exchange group. |
| 2 | Durable cash flow? | Yes. High margins; volume-linked tails. |
| 3 | Bounded bear? | Partial. Bear IRR near zero; state ownership stabilizes but does not eliminate volume risk. |
| 4 | Aligned management? | Mixed. Professional operator; State Treasury 51.8% votes. **[HUMAN REVIEW]** |
| 5 | Cheap vs normalized cash flow? | No. ~25× FY24 earnings at PLN 83.6. |

**Predictive attribute:** none

Return is franchise earnings at price, not a dormant asset or dated catalyst.

## [PROPOSED MEMORY]

## What this business is
Giełda Papierów Wartościowych w Warszawie (Warsaw Stock Exchange, GPW) is the dominant exchange group in Central and Eastern Europe. **[Fact]** The parent company and 16 subsidiaries operate listed equity markets (Main Market, NewConnect), fixed-income platforms (Catalyst, Treasury BondSpot Poland), commodity and energy markets through Towarowa Giełda Energii (TGE), clearing (IRGiT), reference rates and indices (GPW Benchmark), and minority stakes including Armenia Securities Exchange. **[Fact]** Consolidated sales revenue was PLN 464.8 million in FY2024 (+4.5% year over year) and PLN 132.3 million in Q1 2025 (+11.9%). **[Fact]** The group employs roughly 569 people and listed on its own Main Market since November 2010.

## Executive summary
GPW is Poland's dominant exchange croupier: fees on equity, bond, and commodity markets plus recurring data and benchmark revenue through GPW Benchmark. FY2024 revenue was PLN 464.8 million; Q1 2025 hit PLN 132.3 million (+11.9%) with Main Market turnover up 34.6% and cost-to-income at 65.8%, the best in twelve quarters. Commodity gas spot turnover rose 77% in Q1. State Treasury controls 51.8% of votes. At PLN 83.6, base case is **6.61%** per year on PLN 3.35 owner cash, below our 15% band. Dhando is partial (dividend PLN 3.15 proposed for 2024). We propose **watch**; entry near PLN 48 to 52 for ~15% base return.

## Risks & inversion
**Primary risk:** Precious metal price decline combined with delayed development at Canadian Malartic or other large development assets that underpin balance-sheet value.

**Revenue concentration.** 79.7% of FY2025 revenue came from Borborema (23.3%), Côté Gold (27.1%), Cozamin (8.6%), and Vares (20.7%). An operator stoppage, grade issue, or jurisdiction dispute at any one property would materially affect near-term cash. Canadian Malartic alone represents 38.6% of total assets.

**Early-stage cash yield.** Operating cash flow of $6.2 million on ~188 million weighted shares implies ~$0.033 per share, far below the ~$2.77 share price. Even record revenue growth (+55%) does not close the gap without years of compounding or a much lower price.

**Dilution and acquisition risk.** FY2025 equity offering issued 25.9 million shares for $107.2 million gross proceeds. Share count rose to 224.5 million at year-end and 230.8 million by March 18, 2026. Future royalty deals may require more equity if producing cash cannot fund acquisitions.

**Accounting and tax noise.** Reported net loss of $4.1 million includes fair-value gains on the repaid gold-linked loan and other mark-to-market items. Deferred tax liabilities on mineral interests ($134 million) reflect economic royalty value not visible in near-term cash.

**Foreign and market-structure frictions.** 87.4% of revenue from properties outside the U.S.; PFIC status expected for 2025; limited SK1300 reserve disclosure as a royalty company.

**Lens failure mode (optionality):** Using book value (~$3.11/sh equity) or adjusted EBITDA ($9.8M) alone overstates near-term return at today's price. Development royalties may never reach production, and GAAP carrying values do not mark metal-linked economic value.

## Why the market might be wrong
The stock may look like a low-yield micro-cap royalty stub while underpricing a growing producing base plus a large book of non-producing royalties. **[Inference]** FY2025 revenue was concentrated in four mines (Borborema, Côté Gold, Cozamin, Vares = 79.7% of revenue), but Borborema reached commercial production only in 2025 and Canadian Malartic's Odyssey underground project (38.6% of balance-sheet asset weight) is advancing on schedule. **[Inference]** Reported net loss of $4.1 million overstates economic weakness: adjusted EBITDA was a record $9.8 million and adjusted net loss was $1.7 million after stripping fair-value noise on the repaid gold-linked loan and other non-recurring items. **[Inference]** Royalty interests are carried at cost on the balance sheet, so book value (~$3.11 per share at year-end) does not mark portfolio metal exposure or development optionality at spot prices.

## Executive summary
Gold Royalty Corp. is an early-stage precious metals royalty aggregator spun from GoldMining in 2021. FY2025 royalty revenue hit a record $15.6 million (+55%) and operating cash flow turned positive at $6.2 million, but owner cash per share is still only about $0.033 against a $2.77 share price. The company repaid all debt in 2025 and holds $75 million of undrawn revolver capacity, which supports continued royalty acquisitions. Most of the portfolio remains on non-producing assets, including Canadian Malartic's Odyssey project (38.6% of balance-sheet weight). Dhando is partial: no recourse debt helps the floor, but commodity prices and dilution are real tails.

**Base case annual return: -7.41% per year** over seven years on FY2025 operating cash flow per share. Stance: **watch**.

## What this business is
Gold Royalty Corp. (GROY) is a Vancouver-based precious metals royalty and streaming company listed on NYSE American and the TSX. **[Fact]** The company holds a portfolio of gold-focused royalties, streams, and land-agreement interests on mines operated by third parties across the Americas and other regions; it has no mine operating staff and reports in U.S. dollars under IFRS. **[Fact]** GROY was spun out of GoldMining Inc. in 2021 and follows a dual strategy: acquiring cash-flowing royalties and a lower-cost "royalty generator" land model that creates pre-production royalties from surface agreements. **[Fact]** FY2025 royalty revenue was a record $15.6 million (+55% year-over-year), total revenue including land proceeds and interest was $17.8 million, and operating cash flow was $6.2 million on 188.0 million weighted-average shares. **[Fact]** At December 31, 2025 the company had no outstanding debt, $12.4 million cash, and $75.0 million available on its secured revolving credit facility; 224.5 million common shares were outstanding.

Gold Royalty Corp. (GROY) is a Vancouver-based precious metals royalty and streaming company listed on NYSE American and the TSX. **[Fact]** The company holds a portfolio of gold-focused royalties, streams, and land-agreement interests on mines operated by third parties across the Americas and other regions; it has no mine operating staff and reports in U.S. dollars under IFRS. **[Fact]** GROY was spun out of GoldMining Inc. in 2021 and follows a dual strategy: acquiring cash-flowing royalties and a lower-cost "royalty generator" land model that creates pre-production royalties from surface agreements. **[Fact]** FY2025 royalty revenue was a record $15.6 million (+55% year-over-year), total revenue including land proceeds and interest was $17.8 million, and operating cash flow was $6.2 million on 188.0 million weighted-average shares. **[Fact]** At December 31, 2025 the company had no outstanding debt, $12.4 million cash, and $75.0 million available on its secured revolving credit facility; 224.5 million common shares were outstanding.

The stock may look like a low-yield micro-cap royalty stub while underpricing a growing producing base plus a large book of non-producing royalties. **[Inference]** FY2025 revenue was concentrated in four mines (Borborema, Côté Gold, Cozamin, Vares = 79.7% of revenue), but Borborema reached commercial production only in 2025 and Canadian Malartic's Odyssey underground project (38.6% of balance-sheet asset weight) is advancing on schedule. **[Inference]** Reported net loss of $4.1 million overstates economic weakness: adjusted EBITDA was a record $9.8 million and adjusted net loss was $1.7 million after stripping fair-value noise on the repaid gold-linked loan and other non-recurring items. **[Inference]** Royalty interests are carried at cost on the balance sheet, so book value (~$3.11 per share at year-end) does not mark portfolio metal exposure or development optionality at spot prices.

**Predictive attribute:** equity_yield_curve. The company tells shareholders, every quarter, its own best estimate of what they should expect to receive and roughly when (by the 2028 target dissolution date). The market is not required to wait for that date, and with such thin volume, most investors who could buy at $5.80 either do not know the stock exists or cannot build a meaningful position without moving the price.

There is no moat in the traditional sense. Gyrodyne is not trying to defend a competitive position; it is trying to finish selling two properties and close down. The closest thing to a "moat" here is legal and structural: the 2015 shareholder settlement sets a price floor at December 2014 appraised values, and the liquidation-basis accounting rules force the company to disclose, every quarter, its own updated estimate of what shareholders will get. That transparency is unusual for a company this small and this thinly traded, and it is the main reason this name is analyzable at all. **[Inference]**

## What this business is
Gyrodyne, LLC owns two real estate properties left over from a much larger portfolio it has been selling off for two decades. **[Fact]** One is Flowerfield, an industrial park and vacant land in St. James, New York (Suffolk County, Long Island). **[Fact]** The other is Cortlandt Manor, a set of medical office buildings and vacant land in Westchester County. **[Fact]** The company is not trying to grow. It is trying to get government approval to subdivide and improve these properties, sell them for the highest price it can, pay off its debts, and then dissolve and send shareholders the cash. **[Fact]** It reports its books on a "liquidation basis" of accounting, which means the balance sheet already shows management's best estimate of what everything is worth in cash, not the price originally paid for it decades ago. **[Fact]**

**Returns statement:** We expect about **33.4%** per year at $5.80, assuming the company's own disclosed liquidation-basis net asset estimate of $11.79 per share is realized by the December 31, 2028 target date.

## Executive summary
Gyrodyne is winding itself down. It owns two properties on Long Island and in Westchester County, is pursuing zoning approvals to raise their sale value, and intends to dissolve once everything is sold, likely by the end of 2028. The company discloses its own estimate of what shareholders should receive: about $11.79 per share as of March 31, 2026, versus a market price near $5.80. If that estimate holds and the timeline holds, buying today and collecting that amount works out to about **33.4%** per year. We treat this as an asset story, not an earnings story: the return depends on approvals, a pending land sale, and a court appeal, not on growing a business. Even in a slower, costlier case the annualized return still looks positive, so the downside looks bounded but not risk-free given thin trading and litigation. We recommend hold pending human review of the pending appeal and site-plan status, rather than moving to a larger position now.

---

## Risks & inversion
**Primary risk:** The Article 78 court appeal on the Flowerfield subdivision is not yet resolved (10-K FY2025 Item 3, Legal Proceedings), and the company itself says it does not expect to sell Flowerfield until that appeal is decided. An adverse ruling could force a redesign of the subdivision plan, delay the B2K sale beyond the 2028 target, and reduce the ultimate sale price below what is currently assumed in the disclosed NAV.

- **Financing risk:** management states in the 10-K FY2025 MD&A that it may need additional capital to fund operations through the 2028 target date; a dilutive raise would reduce per-share value even if the underlying real estate sells as planned.
- **Liquidity risk:** daily trading volume is often only a few thousand shares (Yahoo Finance trade history), so an investor may not be able to buy or sell a meaningful position near the quoted price.
- **Estimate risk:** the disclosed liquidation NAV in the 10-Q Q1 2026 and 10-K FY2025 has already been revised down once, from $13.91 per share (December 2024) to $11.76 per share (December 2025), as the timeline extended and costs were re-estimated; it could be revised down again.

**Lens failure mode (asset lens):** If the Article 78 appeal fails, the B2K deal collapses entirely, or the liquidation timeline extends materially past 2028 with rising costs, the dated NAV convergence this thesis depends on breaks down, and the stock could instead behave like a distressed, open-ended holding period with a shrinking payoff each year, similar to the bear scenario or worse.

text:
## Why the market might be wrong
The stock may be pricing a full met coal up-cycle while our normalized component base values trough-to-midcycle owner economics closer to **$12 per share** versus a price near **$90**. **[Inference]** Q2 2026 results were strong (revenue **$504 million**, net income **$87 million**, diluted earnings **$1.65** per share), and generalists may extrapolate that quarter into a sustained peak. **[Inference]** The market may also credit Blue Creek development and net cash without applying an explicit supply-response reserve when seaborne met coal prices normalize. **[Inference]** Conversely, if low-cost longwall position and net cash survive a prolonged trough better than smaller peers, the bear case on absolute bankruptcy risk may be too harsh; dhando is partial, not full.

---

#### Catalyst path

- **Near term:** Sustained Q3–Q4 2026 pricing at or above Q2 levels would validate normalization above FY2025 trough.
- **Medium term:** Blue Creek first/second longwall milestones and federal lease execution (8-K Jan 2026).
- **Capital return:** Continuation of quarterly dividend and opportunistic buybacks from net cash **[HUMAN REVIEW]** on policy through the cycle.

## What this business is
Warrior Met Coal is a pure-play producer of premium steelmaking (metallurgical) coal from underground longwall mines in Alabama. **[Fact]** The company operates Mine No. 4, Mine No. 7, and the developing Blue Creek project, and produced **9.3 million metric tons** of steelmaking coal in 2025. **[Fact]** FY2025 revenue was **$1.31 billion**, operating income **$46 million**, net income **$57 million**, and operating cash flow **$229 million** per `HCC/investor-documents/sec-edgar/10-K_20260212_rpt20251231_acc0001193125_26_048914.htm`. **[Fact]** At June 30, 2026 the balance sheet showed **$310 million** of cash (including restricted), **$155 million** of long-term debt, and **$2.29 billion** of stockholders' equity on **52.8 million** shares outstanding per `HCC/investor-documents/sec-edgar/10-Q_20260805_rpt20260630_acc0001193125_26_335324.htm`.

## Why the market might be wrong
The stock still trades like a distressed credit event at roughly **$13** per share (Stooq, 2026-06-03), down sharply from pre-fire levels. **[Inference]** Index and income funds that sort on dividend yield never see the name, which creates a **predictive attribute** (Horizon Kinetics equity yield curve): the payoff is known in direction (regulated recovery, dividend reinstatement, credit repair) but mis-timed for twelve-month holders. **[Inference]** The market may be anchoring on trough GAAP earnings (**$0.71** diluted EPS in FY2025 per 10-K XBRL) instead of mid-cycle owner cash once wildfire payments normalize. **[Opinion]** Patience is the edge; precision on timing and residual liability is not.

---

#### Qualitative adjustments (competition, moat, governance)

## Executive summary
Hawaiian Electric is a regulated Hawaii utility recovering from the 2023 Maui wildfire overhang, with the bank subsidiary sold and the dividend still suspended. At **$13.37** per share, Marvin's base case blends trough FY2025 owner cash with a normalized recovery path and implies about **12.05%** annual return over seven years, below our **~15%** bar. The regulated monopoly and capped downside support a **partial** asymmetric payoff (Pabrai dhando), but residual legal risk and capex keep the moat only **narrow**. **Stance: watch** until dividend policy, credit trajectory, or a cheaper entry clarifies the equity-yield-curve thesis. Horizon Kinetics commentary is noted as **context only**, not in base IRR.

---

### Mental models

- **Regulated monopoly (Munger moat):** Service territory and PUC oversight create pricing power within a band; political and catastrophe risk can break the usual utility calm.
- **Inversion:** What kills the thesis? A new wildfire liability wave, inability to recover costs in rates, or credit stress that blocks capex for grid hardening.
- **Equity yield curve (Horizon Kinetics, context):** Known recovery path, wrong holder horizon; dividend suspension hides the name from yield screens.

## What this business is
Hawaiian Electric Industries is the parent of Hawaii's regulated electric utility and related businesses serving most of the state. **[Fact]** Consolidated revenues were about **$3.09 billion** in fiscal 2025 (`investor-documents/sec-edgar/10-K_20260227_rpt20251231_acc0000354707_26_000008.htm`). **[Fact]** The company reports an **Electric Utility** segment plus **All Other** activities. **[Fact]** Earnings and cash flow are set largely by the Hawaii Public Utilities Commission through allowed returns on rate-base capital, not by open-market pricing alone. **[Fact]** The common dividend has been suspended since the August 2023 Maui wildfires while the company funds legal and restoration obligations. **[Fact]** HE completed the sale of its **90.1%** stake in American Savings Bank at the end of calendar 2024 and is now essentially a pure-play utility (**[Inference]** from Horizon Kinetics Q1 2025 commentary, context tier).

---

### What (Stahl + Lawrence bucket)

**[Fact]** HE operates as a **regulated utility** (Lawrence bucket: regulated_utility): revenues near **$3.1 billion**, with earnings sharing mechanisms that cap both upside and downside versus allowed return on equity. **[Fact]** FY2025 **net income** was about **$126 million** (XBRL), far below FY2024's **$1.4 billion**, which included large settlement-related items. **[Fact]** **Operating cash flow** was about **$391 million** in FY2025 versus **$487 million** in FY2024. **[Fact]** **Stockholders' equity** at the parent was about **$1.61 billion** at December 31, 2025. **[Fact]** **Shares outstanding** about **172.6 million** (Q1 2026 10-Q).

### Business mechanics (Hohn)

**Operating snapshot.** Customers pay regulated electric bills; the utility invests in generation, transmission, and distribution across isolated island grids. Growth comes from rate-base additions (renewables, resilience) approved by regulators, not from volume explosions.

**Thesis pillars.**

1. **Regulated earnings floor:** Allowed ROE frameworks limit downside absent a new catastrophe (**[Fact]** HK Q1 2025 describes earnings-sharing mechanics; **[Fact]** 10-K segment structure).
2. **Liability chapter maturing:** Wildfire settlements and legal reserves reduce tail uncertainty versus 2023-2024 (**[Inference]**; monitor 10-K contingency note each quarter).
3. **Simpler structure:** Bank sale removes dual-regulator complexity and frees capital for the utility (**[Fact]** HK Q1 2025 on Dec 2024 bank sale).
4. **Dividend optionality:** Reinstatement restores the historical income buyer base (**[Inference]**; timing **[Assumption]**).

### Moat (Munger)

**Narrow moat:** geographic monopoly and regulation. **Erosion risk:** political backlash after Maui, climate-related liability, and execution on grid investment. Not **wide** while legal and reputational overhang remain.

## Risks & inversion
**Primary risk:** Specialty-lending borrower default and concentration (76% of gross notes from one borrower, FY2025 10-K) impair notes receivable and segment income.

- **DebtX integration:** Q1 2026 Commercial Loans operating loss and **$5.3M** goodwill require earn-in proof (10-Q).
- **Fee cyclicality:** Auction and NLEX volumes fall in benign credit cycles (10-K MD&A).
- **Tax and corporate drag:** FY2025 effective tax above 25% proxy; corporate overhead **~$5M** absorbs segment profits.
- **Micro-cap liquidity:** Small float limits institutional ownership and can widen bid-ask spreads.

**Lens failure mode (earnings):** If the market prices HGBL as a distressed lender rather than a fee croupier, multiple compression persists despite NLEX cash generation.

## Risks & inversion
**Primary risk:** FDA and state regulators restrict compounded GLP-1 semaglutide marketing and fulfillment, removing a major recent growth driver and compressing gross margin.

Secondary risks:

- **Customer acquisition cost inflation** as weight-loss competition intensifies (Ro, branded drugs, retail clinics).
- **Convertible dilution** on **$974M** notes if stock re-rates lower or conversion triggers.
- **Integration and lease burden** from **$137M** operating lease ROU assets and facility expansion (10-K).

**Lens failure mode (operating):** Treating FY2025 operating cash flow **$300M** as sustainable owner cash without subtracting recurring marketing and growth capex (**$226M** productive asset spend in FY2025).

**Inversion test:** What would make this fail? A finalized FDA ban on mass-marketed compounded semaglutide combined with subscriber churn exceeding new customer adds for two consecutive quarters would break the base growth assumption.

## Risks & inversion
**Primary risk:** **TPL concentration** in client AUM (65% at Dec 31, 2025). A severe TPL drawdown hits fees, performance marketing, and reputation together.

**Inversion (what would make us wrong):**
- Operating owner cash per share is materially higher than $0.59 once proprietary fund economics are attributed to parent shareholders.
- Market is correctly pricing a **catalyst stack** (fund listings, MIAX/HK marks, buybacks) not visible in GAAP operating income.
- Book value compounds quickly enough that price-to-book mean reversion delivers returns without high Lawrence IRR on cash flow.

**Lens failure mode (operating):** Treating consolidated fund **revenue** or **net income** as HKHC owner cash overstates or understates the true per-share economics.

## Executive summary
HKHC is the listed advisory parent of Horizon Kinetics, tied to the FRMO permanent-capital complex. FY2025 showed stronger fee revenue and restored operating profit, but client assets are heavily concentrated in TPL, creating fee beta and reputation risk. Book value is about $18.85 per share; the OTC quote near $27.50 is a premium to GAAP equity. Our base case on operating owner cash of about $0.59 per share implies about **-4.81% per year** over the model horizon at today's price, below our ~15% target. Downside is partially bounded by equity and cash, but not a classic Pabrai "heads I win, tails I don't lose much" at spot. We propose **watch**: understand the Horizon sleeve via FRMO; do not add HKHC on operating cash IRR alone without a lower entry or a catalyst path we can underwrite.

- Crop over-supply years historically compress processor margins faster than costs fall (10-K Risk Factors).

## Why the market might be wrong
There is no dated payoff or structural discount here. **[Inference]** Q1 2026 operating income **$1,665M** (+36% YoY vs **$1,221M**) reflects elevated transaction activity; the market may treat that run rate as permanent. **[Inference]** Our base return uses mid-cycle FY2025 free cash flow per share (**$7.41**), not the Q1 peak. Return is franchise earnings power at price, not a mispricing signal with a known catalyst date.

---

## Risks & inversion
**Primary risk:** **Peak earnings trap** if Q1 2026 energy and rates volumes normalize and the market reapplies a lower multiple on transaction revenue.

- **Regulatory fee caps** on US equities compress take rates.  
- **Mortgage origination slump** stalls Mortgage Technology growth.  
- **Leverage (~$19.6B total debt per FY2025 10-K)** amplifies goodwill risk from Black Knight.

**Inversion:** If we are wrong, ICE remains a high-quality croupier trading at a full multiple with 5–11% returns, not a broken franchise.

## What this business is
Intercontinental Exchange operates global exchange, clearing, and market-data infrastructure plus mortgage-technology workflows. **[Fact]** Customers pay transaction, clearing, listing, and subscription fees across three segments: Exchanges, Fixed Income and Data, and Mortgage Technology. Revenue scales with trading and clearing activity, not balance-sheet lending. **[Fact]** FY2025 net revenues were **$9,931M** with operating income **$4,929M** and net income **$3,315M** (`investor-documents/sec-edgar/10-K_20260205_rpt20251231_acc0001571949_26_000004.htm`). **[Fact]** Q1 2026 net revenues were **$2,977M** (+20% YoY vs **$2,473M**); net income **$1,413M** vs **$797M** (`investor-documents/sec-edgar/10-Q_20260430_rpt20260331_acc0001571949_26_000007.htm`). CEO Jeffrey Sprecher has led the company since its founding.

### Mental models in plain English

**Croupier toll (Stahl):** Does the company earn fees on activity without taking principal risk? **Yes.** Exchange and clearing revenue with high segment margins (`investor-documents/sec-edgar/10-Q_20260430_rpt20260331_acc0001571949_26_000007.htm`).

**Volume vs share (Stahl):** Is handled volume growing faster than share loss? **Yes.** Q1 2026 net revenues **$2,977M** vs **$2,473M** prior-year quarter; Exchanges **$2,470M** vs **$2,123M** (same filing).

**Fee model resilience (Stahl):** Does recurring revenue cushion transaction cyclicality? **Partially.** FI & Data **$657M** and Mortgage Technology **$539M** add recurring layers; Exchanges transaction fees still dominate upside (Q1 2026 10-Q).

**Cycle normalization (Hohn):** Are we underwriting peak activity as normal? **No.** Base free cash flow **$7.41** per share from FY2025, explicitly below the Q1 2026 run rate (`ICE/research/valuation.json`).

The bear case (**5.5%** per year) still implies a positive total return on mid-cycle cash flow, not insolvency. A price near **$115–125** would bring the base case close to **15%** per year. The Hohn screen (about **25–30%** upside with about **10%** downside) **fails** at spot on return alone; downside is **partial** (cyclical earnings, not a balance-sheet blow-up).

section: Why the market might be wrong
text:
## Why the market might be wrong
At **A$0.027** (Yahoo, ~4 Jun 2026), IDA still trades at roughly **56%** of Mar-2026 cash per share (~**A$0.0485**), not the extreme discount to Apr-2025 cash (~**A$0.11**) cited in the sponsor profile. The residual gap likely reflects **Loricatus litigation** (18% of net Tanzania proceeds preserved), **~A$0.9M/quarter legal spend**, exploration burn, and no maiden resource on Minos. The predictive attribute is **post-return cash floor plus legal resolution**: re-rating toward disclosed cash does not require a mine, but further distributions depend on dispute outcomes.

---

#### Thesis pillars

| # | Pillar | Mechanism | Numbers / timeline | Evidence |
|---|--------|-----------|-------------------|----------|
| 1 | Cash floor (post-return) | Treasury still above market cap | A$0.0485/sh vs A$0.027 price | Mar-2026 quarterly |
| 2 | Loricatus reserve | 18% of net Tanzania proceeds preserved | Interest-bearing account pending dispute | Mar-2026 quarterly |
| 3 | Minos option | Drilling on Lake Labyrinth Shear Zone | 2025-26 high-grade intercept ASX releases | `2026-02-16_61312421_RIU_Explorers_Conference_Presentation.pdf` |
| 4 | Legal burn | Arbitration costs run ~A$0.9M/qtr | Erodes cash if unresolved | Mar-2026 quarterly Appendix 5B |

**Fieldwork / management:** Board and CEO bios in company profile (Barnes, Adam, McGuire, Owler). No Marvin site visit.

### What (Stahl + Lawrence bucket)

|-------|-------|----------|
| **Archetype** | optionality | Cash floor + undeveloped ground; no steady owner cash |
| **Lawrence bucket** | other | Pre-revenue explorer |

| **Predictive attribute** | cash_floor_post_return_loricatus_minos | Price below Mar-2026 cash; legal reserve on 18% of settlement |

## Risks & inversion
**Primary risk:** Legal and tax claims on Tanzania settlement cash delay or reduce distributions, turning the cash floor into a melting ice cube.

Additional risks:

- Exploration spend without a maiden resource erodes net cash per share.
- Highly diluted option overhang (20m @ A$0.07 Feb 2026, plus smaller tranches) if the company raises equity despite profile statement of no near-term dilution.
- Sponsor-backed company profile may overweight peer comps and Minos prospectivity.
- 18% Tanzania proceeds preserved: timing and recovery uncertain until Loricatus arbitration concludes.
- Quarterly legal spend near **A$0.9M** can compress cash per share if the dispute drags.
- No maiden Minos resource: geology upside remains unpriced and unproven in filings.

**Lens failure mode (asset / event):** If the market is right that cash is encumbered or will not be returned, the equity is a call on drilling with insufficient funding, not a discount to treasury.

---

- Loricatus arbitration outcome and release of 18% preserved settlement proceeds.
- Mechanical **accumulate** vs **watch** given negative bear IRR if legal burn persists.
- Minos maiden resource timing and whether drilling warrants higher probability in overlay.

Indiana Resources Limited (ASX: IDA) is an Australian mineral explorer focused on the Gawler Craton in South Australia (~5,713 km², 100% owned). The company is pre-revenue; value is driven by treasury cash after the Tanzania Ntaka Hill settlement, ongoing Loricatus arbitration over a preserved slice of proceeds, and the Minos gold program on the Lake Labyrinth Shear Zone. **[Fact]** Aug 2025 capital return of **A$0.05** per share (~**A$32.2M**) is complete; consolidated cash was **A$31.2M** at **31 Mar 2026** per the quarterly Appendix 5B.

At **A$0.027** (Yahoo, ~4 Jun 2026), IDA still trades at roughly **56%** of Mar-2026 cash per share (~**A$0.0485**), not the extreme discount to Apr-2025 cash (~**A$0.11**) cited in the sponsor profile. The residual gap likely reflects **Loricatus litigation** (18% of net Tanzania proceeds preserved), **~A$0.9M/quarter legal spend**, exploration burn, and no maiden resource on Minos. The predictive attribute is **post-return cash floor plus legal resolution**: re-rating toward disclosed cash does not require a mine, but further distributions depend on dispute outcomes.

**Primary risk:** **Multiple compression** if high return on equity is repriced when growth slows or CERC tightens fees.

- **Policy shifts** favor long-term contracts over exchange liquidity.

## Why the market might be wrong
There is no dated structural discount. **[Inference]** Investors may capitalize India's short-term power-market growth and high returns on equity as if they persist at the current earnings multiple without regulatory or competitive pushback. **[Inference]** Our base return uses FY2024 owner cash per share with a small haircut, not a forward run rate from the Q4 FY25 investor deck until the FY2025 annual is on disk. Return is franchise earnings power at price, not a timed mispricing with a known catalyst date.

**Tool:** `python3 _system/scripts/marvin_valuation.py --ticker IEX.NS --write`

## Executive summary
Indian Energy Exchange is a regulated croupier on Indian power and environmental markets: fees on electricity, REC, and gas volume with minimal balance-sheet risk. FY2024 filings show **₹350.8 crore** revenue and about **₹302.5 crore** profit after tax; the Q4 FY25 presentation points to continued volume growth but is not in our starting cash flow until the FY2025 annual is filed. At **₹124.07** per share (Yahoo, 2026-06-04), we expect about **9.74% per year** over 7 years on **₹3.2** normalized owner cash per share (below our portfolio hurdle for a core add). Asymmetric payoff (Pabrai dhando) stays **partial** because volume and fee regulation are cyclical and political. Gas and derivatives adoption are embedded in the growth path, not separate option terminals. We propose **watch** and would revisit nearer **₹95–100** where Lawrence base case approaches a mid-teens annual return.

---

- **Base catalyst** (7 years): Mid-cycle owner cash; exit near **35 times** year-10 cash flow

**Disruption / competitive watch:** New exchange licenses; CERC fee cuts; state-discom bypass of markets; gas market slow adoption.

## Why the market might be wrong
The market may be pricing INV as a thin, cash-burning holding company rather than as a claim on Accelsius's cooling franchise if two-phase cooling becomes required as chip power rises. The predictive attribute is commercial adoption of Accelsius systems at hyperscalers and high-density sites, not near-term consolidated earnings. Inefficiency comes from complexity: multi-entity capital structure, preferreds and noncontrolling interests, and a short public history after the Learn CW business combination.

section: Why the market might be wrong
text:
## Why the market might be wrong
Yield-oriented investors may treat KRP as a simple bond proxy and miss the embedded acreage option on **~12.3 million gross mineral acres** and **~4.7 million gross ORRI acres**, with more than half of aggregate acreage in the Permian and Mid-Continent. **[Inference]** Screeners that rank on trailing GAAP earnings rather than cash distributions understate owner yield because depreciation and acquisition accounting suppress net income per unit relative to cash paid. **[Inference]** The partnership's **$441.5 million** revolver balance and Apollo-affiliated preferred equity may be priced as permanent leverage overhang rather than as financing for accretive acquisitions that expand the royalty footprint. **[Inference]** Q1 2026 revenue and earnings softness may be extrapolated as structural when FY2025 production still rose to **25,760 Boe/d** (`10-K_20260226`).

---

## [PROPOSED MEMORY]
- [PROPOSED COMPANY] KRP: first filing-grounded dive 2026-06-11; FY2025 ~$1.60/unit distributions on 93.4M units; $441.5M revolver; 72,944 MBoe proved reserves; ~12.3M gross mineral acres.

## Executive summary
Kimbell Royalty Partners is a passive U.S. mineral and royalty owner that pays monthly cash distributions while growing through bolt-on acquisitions funded with equity and revolver debt. FY2025 revenues were **$333.8 million**, distributions about **$1.60** per unit, and proved reserves **72,944 MBoe** with production **25,760 Boe/d**. The partnership had **$441.5 million** drawn on a **$625 million** secured revolver at year-end 2025, which limits dhando versus debt-free royalty peers. At **$15.52** per unit and **$1.60** starting owner cash, Marvin's base case is **12.6% per year** over seven years, below our **~15%** target, so stance is **watch**. Q1 2026 revenue and earnings per unit fell year over year; we use FY2025 distribution run-rate in the base case. No approved third-party sources are in the base IRR. Undeveloped net acres are an overlay option only.

Yield-oriented investors may treat KRP as a simple bond proxy and miss the embedded acreage option on **~12.3 million gross mineral acres** and **~4.7 million gross ORRI acres**, with more than half of aggregate acreage in the Permian and Mid-Continent. **[Inference]** Screeners that rank on trailing GAAP earnings rather than cash distributions understate owner yield because depreciation and acquisition accounting suppress net income per unit relative to cash paid. **[Inference]** The partnership's **$441.5 million** revolver balance and Apollo-affiliated preferred equity may be priced as permanent leverage overhang rather than as financing for accretive acquisitions that expand the royalty footprint. **[Inference]** Q1 2026 revenue and earnings softness may be extrapolated as structural when FY2025 production still rose to **25,760 Boe/d** (`10-K_20260226`).

## Why the market might be wrong
The market may treat LAND as a passive high-yield REIT whose dividend is fully covered by recurring rent, missing the portfolio rotation and lease-repositioning story underway in 2025–2026. **[Fact]** Management sold **13 farms** (**12,502** acres) for **~$95.4 million** in FY2025, recognizing **~$21.3 million** of net gains, and modified leases on "Repositioned Farms" to trade lower fixed base rent for higher participation on permanent crops (including a **~$4.9 million** pistachio bonus payment in Q1 2026). **[Inference]** At **~$9.23** (June 10, 2026), the stock trades at roughly **44%** below GAAP book equity of **~$16.50** per share, a discount consistent with small-cap REIT yield-screen exclusion and concern that the monthly dividend exceeds normalized cash earnings. **[Inference]** Predictive attribute: **farmland lease REIT** plus **market structure discount** (externally managed, preferred equity layer, monthly payout cadence).

## Executive summary
Gladstone Land is a diversified U.S. farmland landlord: triple-net leases on row and permanent crops, California water rights, and an active sell-and-reinvest rotation program. FY2025 AFFO of **$0.393** per share covered only **~70%** of the **$0.56** annual dividend; Q1 2026 coverage fell to **~54%** as fixed base rent declined after dispositions while participation rent remained lumpy. Leverage is manageable (**~$486 million** total indebtedness, mostly fixed-rate) but Q1 ATM issuance added **3.7 million** shares. At **~$9.23**, our base case annual return is **2.2%** per year on normalized owner cash of **$0.38** per share (seven-year model, **14×** exit multiple). Book equity provides a partial floor, but external adviser fees and dividend coverage risk prevent a full dhando classification. We propose **watch** pending proof that participation rents and reinvested sale proceeds restore AFFO above the dividend.

Gladstone Land Corporation is an externally managed real estate investment trust that owns and leases farmland to independent farmers across the United States. **[Fact]** At December 31, 2025 the portfolio comprised **144 farms** totaling approximately **98,688** gross acres in **14 states**, plus roughly **55,532** acre-feet of California water assets ( **55,649** acre-feet at March 31, 2026). **[Fact]** The company earns revenue primarily from triple-net leases (tenants pay property taxes, insurance, and maintenance), participation rents tied to crop prices and yields, and occasional direct-operated crop sales on a small subset of farms. **[Fact]** FY2025 total operating revenue was **$88.3 million**; adjusted funds from operations were **$0.393** per diluted share; the company paid a monthly dividend of **$0.0467** per share (**$0.5604** annualized). **[Fact]** Gladstone Management Corporation, controlled by David Gladstone, serves as external adviser under a contract charging **0.60%** per year of gross tangible real estate plus incentive fees above a **7.0%** annualized hurdle on adjusted common equity.

The market may treat LAND as a passive high-yield REIT whose dividend is fully covered by recurring rent, missing the portfolio rotation and lease-repositioning story underway in 2025–2026. **[Fact]** Management sold **13 farms** (**12,502** acres) for **~$95.4 million** in FY2025, recognizing **~$21.3 million** of net gains, and modified leases on "Repositioned Farms" to trade lower fixed base rent for higher participation on permanent crops (including a **~$4.9 million** pistachio bonus payment in Q1 2026). **[Inference]** At **~$9.23** (June 10, 2026), the stock trades at roughly **44%** below GAAP book equity of **~$16.50** per share, a discount consistent with small-cap REIT yield-screen exclusion and concern that the monthly dividend exceeds normalized cash earnings. **[Inference]** Predictive attribute: **farmland lease REIT** plus **market structure discount** (externally managed, preferred equity layer, monthly payout cadence).

## Risks & inversion
**Primary risk:** Residential HVAC volumes stay weak longer than price/mix can offset, while the stock remains priced for mid-single-digit per-share cash growth.

- **Volume cyclicality:** Home Comfort sales fell **7%** in 2025 on **17%** volume decline; Q1 2026 Home Comfort segment profit **$86.5M** vs **$95.6M** prior year.
- **Working capital swings:** Operating cash flow fell to **$758M** from **$946M** in 2024; timing can distort year-on-year FCF.
- **Leverage:** Long-term debt **$1,144M** plus commercial paper **$226M** at year-end 2025; book debt-to-capital **54%**.
- **Regulatory transition:** Refrigerant and efficiency rules require product redesign and dealer training; execution risk during transitions.
- **Inversion (Munger):** What kills the thesis? Two years of negative Home Comfort volume with inability to raise price would force bear-case growth and erode moat toward **eroding**.

**Lens failure mode (operating):** If housing-linked volumes weaken more than replacement demand supports, owner cash growth understates bear risk at today's multiple.

## Why the market might be wrong
The market may treat Lennox as a peak-cycle HVAC name and underweight its pricing power, buyback discipline, and the offset from Building Climate. **[Fact]** Consolidated gross margin rose 10 basis points to **33.4%** in 2025 despite a **13%** volume decline, as **9%** price and mix partially offset volumes. **[Fact]** The company repurchased **$482 million** of stock in 2025 (versus **$54 million** in 2024) and raised the dividend to **$4.55** per share from **$4.36**. **[Inference]** Generalists may anchor on Home Comfort volume weakness (sales down **7%** in 2025) and Q1 2026 earnings softness (diluted EPS **$3.35** versus **$3.63** in Q1 2025) and miss that Building Climate grew segment profit **9%** and management is returning capital at scale. At **~$552** per share, however, the stock prices in much of that quality: there is no dated catalyst; the inefficiency is **descriptive** (premium compounder above our return hurdle), not an equity yield curve setup.

## Risks & inversion
**Primary risk:** Paying a premium multiple for a quality oligopoly while debt-funded buybacks raise leverage into an industrial downturn, leaving equity with low returns despite stable operations.

- **Leverage:** Long-term debt rose **35%** in FY2025 to **$20.7 billion** while repurchasing **$4.6 billion** of stock (10-K FY2025).
- **Cyclical volumes:** Merchant and packaged gas volumes track industrial production; recession would slow growth assumptions.
- **Capital intensity:** Capital spending **$5.3 billion** must stay productive to sustain **$10+** free cash flow per share.
- **Inversion (Munger):** What kills the thesis? Two years of flat owner cash per share while buybacks continue above **$4 billion** and the stock stays above **35 times** free cash flow would force bear-case growth and erode dhando to **none**.

**Lens failure mode (operating):** If normalized owner cash stalls near **$11** per share while the stock stays above **$450**, the market is paying infrastructure scarcity prices without enough per-share cash growth to clear a **15%** return hurdle.

Linde plc (LIN) is the world's largest industrial gases company, formed from the 2018 merger of Praxair and Linde AG. **[Fact]** It sells atmospheric and specialty gases through on-site plants (long take-or-pay contracts), merchant bulk delivery, and packaged cylinders to customers in manufacturing, healthcare, electronics, chemicals, and energy. **[Fact]** FY2025 sales were **$34.0 billion** (+3% versus FY2024), with four reportable segments: Americas, APAC, EMEA, and Linde Engineering. **[Fact]** CEO Sanjiv Lamba leads an Irish-domiciled company listed on Nasdaq; headquarters are in the United Kingdom and United States.

The market may treat Linde as a bond-proxy quality compounder and pay a premium multiple for oligopoly stability, underweighting that **$4.6 billion** of FY2025 share repurchases and rising long-term debt (**$20.7 billion** versus **$15.3 billion** prior year) compress future per-share growth if industrial volumes soften. **[Inference]** Generalists may anchor on adjusted earnings growth (+7% FY2025 diluted earnings per share) while the stock trades near **49 times** GAAP free cash flow per share at **$531.30**, leaving little margin of safety. **[Fact]** Q1 2026 sales rose **8%** and diluted earnings per share **13%**, so near-term fundamentals are strong; there is no dated predictive attribute, only a **descriptive** premium-multiple setup.

section: Why the market might be wrong

## Why the market might be wrong
There is **no classic dated mispricing signal** (HK predictive attribute: **none**). **[Inference]** Generalists may anchor on trailing free cash flow (~**$10** per share) without adjusting for a temporary capex super-cycle: FY2025 capital spending rose **55%** to **$7.8 billion** to build injectable and oral capacity. **[Fact]** Q1 2026 revenue was **$19.8 billion** (+**55.5%** year over year) with Mounjaro global **$8.7 billion** and Zepbound **$4.2 billion** in the quarter. **[Fact]** Trulicity U.S. revenue was **$5.4 billion** FY2025, down from prior peaks as patients switch to tirzepatide. **[Inference]** The market may be **right on quality** but **wrong on entry price**: at about **$1,187** per share, investors pay roughly **119 times** normalized owner cash, leaving little margin of safety even if tirzepatide growth persists. Return here is **owner cash at price through the capacity cycle**, not a sum-of-the-parts on pipeline optionality alone.

---

Pillars 1–2 are **structural** (GLP-1 cycle). Pillars 3–4 provide ** diversification** but are smaller than tirzepatide today.

## Executive summary
Lilly is the clearest large-cap beneficiary of the GLP-1/GIP obesity and diabetes cycle. FY2025 operating cash flow was **$16.8 billion**; after **$7.8 billion** of capital spending, owner cash is about **$9.98 per share**. Q1 2026 revenue was **$19.8 billion** (+**55.5%** year over year), with net income **$7.4 billion** (diluted earnings per share **$8.26**).

At about **$1,187** (Yahoo Finance, 2026-07-10), the Lawrence base case implies about **-7.3% per year** on normalized owner cash, below our **15%** accumulate hurdle. The business has a **widening** durable advantage (Munger moat) on tirzepatide clinical data and manufacturing scale, with **partial** asymmetric payoff (Pabrai dhando): extraordinary revenue growth and **$7.3 billion** cash, but premium multiple and **~$42.5 billion** of debt limit downside protection at spot. ## Risks & inversion
**Primary risk:** **Tirzepatide growth decelerates or margins compress** before the capex cycle converts to normalized free cash flow, leaving investors holding a premium multiple on peak growth expectations.

- **Competition:** Novo Nordisk and oral GLP-1 developers can erode share or force pricing concessions (10-K risk factors).
- **Manufacturing and supply:** Capacity constraints have been a bottleneck; execution risk remains on new site ramp (10-K; capex **$7.8B** FY25).
- **Regulatory pricing:** U.S. Inflation Reduction Act negotiation and international reference pricing can cap net pricing power (10-K).
- **Legacy erosion:** Trulicity U.S. **$5.4B** FY2025 shows how quickly a GLP-1 franchise can fade when superseded.
- **Leverage:** Long-term debt **~$42.5B** is serviceable at current earnings but limits flexibility if growth stalls (10-K balance sheet).

**Inversion:** If we are wrong, Lilly is the winning GLP-1/GIP compounder priced for perfection: you own the best franchise in the largest drug category in history, and normalized owner cash catches up to the multiple over many years.

**Lens failure mode:** Operating lens fails if pipeline readouts (oral GLP-1, retatrutide) become the dominant value driver beyond what Lawrence base growth assumes. Current filings support staying on the operating lens with pipeline upside in bull scenario only.

## Why the market might be wrong
The market may price Limoneira as a cyclical lemon packer whose revenue fell **17%** year over year, missing the dated cash from **~$180 million** of expected development distributions and episodic water and land sales. **[Inference]** At **~$11.83**, the stock sits near GAAP book while **10,500** California acres, basin water rights, and entitled housing land are carried at historical cost. **[Fact]** Management reiterates a strategic pivot: Sunkist lemon partnership (shifting quarterly revenue cadence), **800** acres of non-bearing avocados coming into production, **~$10 million** targeted selling, general, and administrative savings, and near-term water monetization in fiscal 2026. **[Inference]** Predictive attribute: **land, water, and development yield curve** (known catalyst stack with lumpy ag transition noise).

## Risks & inversion
**Primary risk:** Sunkist transition and citrus margin compression extend the cash-from-operations trough while development distributions slip, leaving equity exposed to **~$90M** debt without ag cash cover.

- **Inversion:** If lemon volumes hit **4.0–4.5M** cartons at stable pricing and Harvest distributions track the management table, the equity yield curve compresses toward book-plus-cash NAV without heroic ag growth.
- Housing slowdown in Ventura County could delay Harvest Phase 2 absorption.
- Drought, HLB, or avocado crop failure would impair the growth pillar tied to **800** bearing acres.
- Regulatory delay on East Areas I and II (cited in 10-K risk factors) could push development cash right on the curve.

**Lens failure mode (asset payoff):** If development proceeds are overstated or debt-funded land spending rises without distributions, the asset lens collapses to a low-return ag compounder at trough cash flow.

## Executive summary
Alliant Energy is a Midwest regulated utility compounding rate base through a large renewables, storage, and gas build-out while paying a growing dividend. FY2025 earnings per share reached **$3.15** on **$4.36 billion** of revenue; Q1 2026 earnings per share of **$0.87** rose **5%** year over year. At **$75.70** per share (Yahoo close, July 9, 2026), Marvin's base case implies about **5.47%** annual return over seven years on starting owner cash of **$3.15** per share, well below our **~15%** bar. The regulated franchise supports a **narrow** moat and **partial** asymmetric payoff (regulated floor, but interest-rate and execution risk on **$10.95 billion** of long-term debt). **Stance: watch** until either a cheaper entry or clearer proof that data-center load converts to authorized returns faster than the Iowa moratorium allows. No approved third-party sources inform base IRR.

## Why the market might be wrong
The stock trades like a bond-proxy utility: investors buy the **2.8%** dividend yield at **$75.70** and credit quality, not a growth franchise. **[Inference]** That framing may underprice the rate-base growth embedded in **$3.1 billion+** annual capital spending and data-center interconnection agreements disclosed in the 10-K. **[Inference]** Conversely, the market may be right that the **IPL retail electric base-rate moratorium** through September 2029 caps near-term Iowa earnings acceleration even as capital spending rises. **[Opinion]** There is no dated mispricing catalyst; the edge, if any, is patience on a regulated compounding path at a full (not cheap) price.
